summary: A complete target-level planning pass for DM.0–DM.8: 123 stable targets imported from the accepted parts with full reconciled contracts, plus 11 missing rational-category, Anderson-comparison and ABP arithmetic targets. Every layer is planned, with precise unresolved proof and supplier boundaries; no layer is closed and no target is claimed implemented. The full reader carries all 134 contracts, while the compact Suggested file contains only light definitions and milestones statable over pinned native carriers.

nodes.title: Rational pre-t-motives
nodes.statement: A pre-t-motive is a finite-dimensional vector space P over k̄(t), where k̄ is the chosen algebraic closure of k=F_q(θ), with a bijective additive σ_P satisfying σ_P(ap)=a^(−1)σ_P(p); the coefficient twist is inverse q-Frobenius and fixes t. A morphism is a k̄(t)-linear map commuting with these operators. For basis columns p and q with σp=Φ_Pp and σq=Φ_Qq, a morphism p↦Bq satisfies B^(−1)Φ_Q=Φ_PB. The category is F_q(t)-linear. Its tensor product has diagonal σ; its unit is k̄(t) with coefficient σ; internal Hom carries ρ↦σ_Q∘ρ∘σ_P^(−1). The dual has matrix (Φ_P^(−1))^tr. For every integer n, C(n) is the rank-one object with matrix (t−θ)^n, with C(0) the unit and C(n)⊗C(m)≅C(n+m).
hypotheses: q=p^m, m>0, and θ is transcendental over F_q. The inverse Frobenius is algebraic; no analytic field is required.
proofSteps: Extend the pinned perfect-field Frobenius equivalence to the polynomial ring and then its fraction field, fixing t.
Use finite-dimensional vector spaces with semilinear automorphisms, equivalently modules over k̄(t)[σ,σ^(−1)]; a separate implementation of a skew Laurent ring is not needed to state the category.
Compute tensor and internal-Hom actions from semilinearity. Evaluation and coevaluation commute with σ; inverse transpose is forced by preserving their pairing.

For the scalar fixed field, write a rational function in coprime numerator/monic-denominator form. Uniqueness makes both coefficient vectors Frobenius-fixed, so the fixed field is F_q(t), without using analytic fixed-field theory.
acceptance: If p=Bq, verify Φ_P=σ(B)Φ_Q B_inv, where B_inv is the ordinary matrix inverse and σ(B) is coefficient twisting.
Verify evaluation and coevaluation with the inverse-transpose matrix.

nodes.title: Rationalization of effective dual t-motives
nodes.statement: For a broad effective dual t-motive H finite free over k̄[t], with inverse-Frobenius semilinear σ and (t−θ)^s H contained in σH for some s≥0, put H_rat=k̄(t)⊗_(k̄[t])H and give it diagonal σ. This is a pre-t-motive: σ becomes bijective after localization. Polynomial intertwiners induce rational morphisms and composition is preserved. For an Anderson dual motive, which is in addition finite free over k̄[σ], rationalization agrees with Papanikolas’s functor. The statement does not infer this extra Ore freeness from the broad effective condition. Rationalization preserves tensor products whenever the corresponding effective tensor product is in the chosen category.
hypotheses: H is finite free over k̄[t] and satisfies the effective characteristic-support condition; k̄ is perfect. The Anderson subcategory adds finite freeness over k̄[σ].
proofSteps: The support condition makes the σ-linearization a square full-rank matrix with determinant c(t−θ)^s for some nonzero c and s≥0; localizing makes it invertible.
Extend the semilinear operator and each morphism by the localization universal property. The tensor compatibility is the standard tensor/localization comparison.
The Hom map after tensoring with F_q(t) is fully faithful for Anderson objects by the outgoing constant-denominator theorem in DM.8; no such fullness is assumed in constructing rationalization.
acceptance: Do not identify polynomial morphisms with all rationalized morphisms: 1/t on the unit rational object requires a denominator.

nodes.title: Rigid abelian category of pre-t-motives
nodes.statement: The category of pre-t-motives is a rigid abelian F_q(t)-linear tensor category, with End(unit)=F_q(t) and finite-dimensional Hom spaces. Kernels and cokernels are computed in k̄(t)-vector spaces with the induced bijective semilinear actions. This category is not asserted neutral Tannakian: a fibre functor is constructed only for its rigid analytically trivial subcategory in DM.8.
proofSteps: Kernel and image stability follow from equivariance, and bijectivity descends to kernels and quotients; finite-dimensionality is preserved.
The tensor and internal-Hom constructions give duals via the ordinary evaluation and coevaluation maps.

A minimal dependence among fixed elements of internal Hom, normalized to have a coefficient 1, becomes a shorter dependence after applying σ and subtracting; hence its coefficients lie in F_q(t). Thus a fixed-field independent family remains k̄(t)-independent, bounding Hom dimension by the dimension of internal Hom. This algebraic argument requires no analytic DM.8 target.
acceptance: Check the zero object, C(n) duality and exact kernels in matrix coordinates.
The full pre-t-motive category is not silently identified with Papanikolas’s generated category T.

sources.match: Abelianness, finite Hom and rigid tensor structure over the exact rational constant field.

nodes.title: Anderson uniformization and analytic triviality
nodes.statement: Let E be an abelian t-module over C∞ in generic characteristic with normalized exponential exp_E and associated contravariant τ-motive M(E). Then exp_E is surjective if and only if M(E) is rigid analytically trivial: if τm=Θm, there is Υ∈GL_r(T) satisfying Υ=Υ^(1)Θ. For E descending to k̄, through the τ-to-σ star dictionary and its associated Anderson dual motive H(E), this is equivalent to the rationalized dual pre-t-motive being rigid analytically trivial, with Ψ^(−1)=ΦΨ. For general C∞ coefficients the same dual criterion uses the analogous difference modules over C∞(t), rather than pretending that E descends to k̄. The rank-r A-period lattice and a Betti basis correspond under Anderson’s comparison. In particular the Carlitz tensor power C^⊗n is uniformizable for every n≥1: its dual fundamental solution is Ω^n, while its τ trivialization is ((t−θ)Ω)^n. The two matrices use different conventions.
hypotheses: E is abelian and defined over C∞ with θ transcendental, ||θ||=q. The assertion is not made for arbitrary nonabelian t-modules or broad effective dual motives. The dual object is the one matched to E by DM.4, not an arbitrary transpose of a τ matrix.
proofSteps: Apply Anderson’s analytic comparison between the exponential sequence and the τ-invariant basis of the Tate realization; identify the comparison map and its rank.
Transport along the star anti-isomorphism and the abelian dual realization, retaining the variance and ordinary-matrix-inverse versus coefficient-twist distinction.

For the Carlitz case, Ω^(−1)=(t−θ)Ω makes Ω^n a σ-solution; applying positive twist shows Υ=((t−θ)Ω)^n satisfies Υ=Υ^(1)(t−θ)^n. Integral and rational rigid triviality agree by the polynomial determinant-support theorem.
acceptance: For the Carlitz rank-one τ motive use (t−θ)Ω, whereas for its dual σ motive use Ω.
Check n=2, rank one and group dimension two.
Keep the original analytic comparison proof as an explicit source gap until inspected; the survey statement alone does not close it.

sources.match: States Anderson’s abelian t-module comparison and distinguishes the τ and dual σ conventions.

nodes.title: Conjugate size for the ABP arithmetic setting
nodes.statement: Write k=F_q(θ), A=F_q[θ], |θ|∞=q, fix a finite separable extension K0/k of degree d, and put K=∪_(ν≥0)K0^(q^(−ν)), O the integral closure of A in K, and O0=O∩K0. All fields are embedded in the chosen k̄⊂C∞. For x∈k̄ define S(x) as the maximum of |τx|∞ over its k-conjugates, with S(0)=0; define polynomial and finite-matrix size by the maximum coefficient size, using zero for an empty array. Size is ultrametric and submultiplicative and S(x^(n))=S(x)^(q^n) for every integer twist n. For 0≠x∈O, S(x)≥1 and |x|∞≥S(x)^(1−d). The exponent uses the separable degree d of K0, not the infinite degree of K/k.
proofSteps: The finite set of distinct conjugates gives a maximum; pure inseparability contributes no new conjugates.
For x∈O0, the product over conjugates is a nonzero polynomial in θ. At the chosen infinity norm it is at least 1, giving the lower bound on one factor.
Raise any x∈O to a sufficiently large q-power in O0 and take roots of both inequalities. The coefficient and matrix bounds follow from the ultrametric triangle inequality.
acceptance: Retain max over all conjugates, including extensions with different infinity embeddings.

sources.match: Conjugate size and the integral lower bound, including passage to the perfect closure.

nodes.title: ABP Liouville inequality
nodes.statement: Write k=F_q(θ), A=F_q[θ], |θ|∞=q, fix a finite separable extension K0/k of degree d, and put K=∪_(ν≥0)K0^(q^(−ν)), O the integral closure of A in K, and O0=O∩K0. All fields are embedded in the chosen k̄⊂C∞. Let f(Z)=Σ a_i Z^i∈O[Z] be nonzero, and let λ∈k̄ be a nonzero root of exact multiplicity ν≥1. Then |λ|∞^ν≥(max_i S(a_i))^(−d).
proofSteps: If |λ|∞≥1, use max_i S(a_i)≥1. Otherwise remove the power of Z dividing f so that its constant coefficient is nonzero; this does not change the multiplicity at λ.
Expand f(Z+λ), whose first ν coefficients vanish. Evaluate at Z=−λ and use the ultrametric bound on the remaining coefficients.
Apply the integral lower bound to the nonzero constant coefficient and divide by the maximal coefficient size.
acceptance: For f=Z−θ and K0=k, check q≥q^(−1).
For f=(Z−1)^ν the bound is equality 1; λ=0 is explicitly excluded.

sources.match: The multiplicity and separable degree occur exactly in this lower bound.

nodes.title: ABP bounded-element count
nodes.statement: Write k=F_q(θ), A=F_q[θ], |θ|∞=q, fix a finite separable extension K0/k of degree d, and put K=∪_(ν≥0)K0^(q^(−ν)), O the integral closure of A in K, and O0=O∩K0. All fields are embedded in the chosen k̄⊂C∞. For every real C>1, the finite set B_ν(C)={x∈O0^(q^(−ν)):S(x)≤C} satisfies lim_(ν→∞) #B_ν(C)^(1/(q^ν d))=C. If k0 is the full finite constant field of K0, f=[k0:F_q], and D∞=Σ_(v|∞)e_v v on its smooth proper curve, then f·deg_(k0)(D∞)=d. For all sufficiently large integral n, {x∈O0:S(x)≤q^n}=L(nD∞) and its cardinality is q^(dn+f(1−g)). No exact-constant-field assumption k0=F_q is imposed.
proofSteps: Use the finite-normalization/place dictionary to identify integrality away from infinity and S(x)≤q^n with ord_v(x)≥−n e_v for every place above infinity. Use the exact full constant field k0 when applying Riemann–Roch.
The fundamental degree formula gives f deg_(k0)D∞=d; pinned high-degree Riemann–Roch and finite-dimensional-space cardinality give the displayed exact large-n count.
The q^ν-power map identifies B_ν(q^δ) with the ball of radius q^(q^νδ) in O0 when q^νδ is integral. Take the normalized root and then squeeze arbitrary C>1 between such radii.
acceptance: For K0=k, B_ν(q^δ) has q^(floor(q^νδ)+1) elements, so its normalized root tends to q^δ.
For K0=F_(q^f)(θ), d=f and g=0; the exponent is f(n+1), not fn+1.

sources.match: Normalized cardinality limit from Riemann–Roch; the exact-constant-field factor is made explicit for the pinned interface.

nodes.title: ABP Thue–Siegel kernel bound
nodes.statement: Write k=F_q(θ), A=F_q[θ], |θ|∞=q, fix a finite separable extension K0/k of degree d, and put K=∪_(ν≥0)K0^(q^(−ν)), O the integral closure of A in K, and O0=O∩K0. All fields are embedded in the chosen k̄⊂C∞. For C>1 and integers 0<r<s, if M∈Mat_(r×s)(O) has S(M)<C, there is a nonzero x∈O^s with Mx=0 and S(x)<C^(r/(s−r)).
proofSteps: Choose C′ strictly between max(1,S(M)) and C and ε>0 small enough that (1+ε)(C′)^(r/(s−r))<C^(r/(s−r)).
At a sufficiently deep common q-root level the matrix entries belong to O0^(q^(−ν)). The count theorem makes the source ball contain more vectors than its image ball.
Subtract two vectors with the same image. The ultrametric bound gives the strict size estimate, with no extra factor 2.
acceptance: For the zero 1×2 matrix, a coordinate vector has size 1<C.
The hypotheses r<s and C>1 are essential; no nonzero kernel is claimed for the identity square matrix.

sources.match: Strict coefficient-size kernel bound over the perfect-closure integral ring.

nodes.title: ABP polynomial Thue–Siegel bound
nodes.statement: Write k=F_q(θ), A=F_q[θ], |θ|∞=q, fix a finite separable extension K0/k of degree d, and put K=∪_(ν≥0)K0^(q^(−ν)), O the integral closure of A in K, and O0=O∩K0. All fields are embedded in the chosen k̄⊂C∞. For C>1 and integers 0<r<s, if M∈Mat_(r×s)(O[t]) has S(M)<C, there is a nonzero polynomial column x∈O[t]^s with Mx=0 and S(x)<C^(r/(s−r)). There is no uniform degree bound in this statement. For any d0≥deg_t M, choose e large enough that r′=r(d0+e+1)<s′=s(e+1) and S(M)<C′=C^((r/(s−r))/(r′/(s′−r′))); the construction then gives deg_t x≤e.
proofSteps: Encode multiplication by M from columns of degree≤e to columns of degree≤d0+e as a matrix over O of shape r′×s′, with the same coefficient-size bound.
As e grows, r′/(s′−r′) tends to r/(s−r), so the strict hypothesis S(M)<C permits the displayed choice of C′.
Apply the scalar kernel bound at C′ and decode coefficients to obtain both the stated degree cutoff for this choice and the final size bound.
acceptance: For M=(1,t), x=(−t,1) gives the expected polynomial kernel.
For a constant matrix, recover the scalar result.

sources.match: Polynomial coefficient expansion, retaining the strict bound without inventing a degree-uniform result.

nodes.title: ABP auxiliary polynomial row
nodes.statement: Under the normalized integral hypotheses below, choose B>1 larger than |θ|∞^(a+2δ)·max(1,S(Θ))^(q/(q−1))·max(1,S(ϑ)), and put H=B^(2(ℓ−1)). For every positive integer N divisible by 2ℓ there exists h_N∈O[t]^(1×ℓ), h_N≠0, deg_t h_N<aN and S(h_N)<H, such that E_N=h_Nψ vanishes at θ^(q^(−(N+j))) for 0≤j<N. One may choose h_N to satisfy h_N Θ Θ^(−1)…Θ^(−(N+j−1)) ϑ^(−(N+j)), evaluated at t=θ^(q^(−(N+j))), equals zero for each such j. These are polynomial-row constraints, not evaluations of a formal series outside its convergence domain.
hypotheses: Write k=F_q(θ), A=F_q[θ], |θ|∞=q, fix a finite separable extension K0/k of degree d, and put K=∪_(ν≥0)K0^(q^(−ν)), O the integral closure of A in K, and O0=O∩K0. All fields are embedded in the chosen k̄⊂C∞.

Fix ℓ>1, Φ∈Mat_ℓ(O[t]) with detΦ=c(t−θ)^s, c∈O nonzero, s≥0; ψ∈E^ℓ satisfies ψ^(−1)=Φψ. Fix 0≠ρ∈O^(1×ℓ) with ρψ(θ)=0, and ϑ∈Mat_(ℓ×(ℓ−1))(O) of rank ℓ−1 with ρϑ=0. Put Θ=adj(Φ), a=1−1/(2ℓ), and δ=deg_t Θ≥0.
proofSteps: The adjugate identity ΦΘ=c(t−θ)^sI iterated under σ expresses the constrained rows as a nonzero scalar polynomial times E_N. At the specified point the scalar is nonzero and ρψ(θ)=0 supplies the annihilator condition.
Encode the constraints as r=(ℓ−1)N equations in s0=(ℓ−1/2)N coefficients of h_N. Their matrix has size at most |θ|∞^(q^(−N)(aN+2Nδ))·S(Θ)^(q/(q−1))·S(ϑ), bounded strictly by B since N/q^N≤1.
The scalar Siegel theorem gives size <B^(r/(s0−r))=H. This fixes a uniform constant independent of N and discharges the auxiliary constant-level planning obligation.
acceptance: Check the equation/unknown ratio r/(s0−r)=2(ℓ−1), independent of N.
The case ℓ=1 is handled directly in lifting and is excluded here; N divisible by 2ℓ makes all degree cutoffs integral.

sources.match: Integral normalization, adjugate constraints and bounded coefficient systems; the displayed B is a coarse explicit bound on the source estimate.

nodes.title: Vanishing of the ABP auxiliary entire function
nodes.statement: Under DM.8/abp-auxiliary, for every sufficiently large positive multiple N of 2ℓ, every chosen row h_N satisfying the stated constraints and S(h_N)≤H has h_Nψ=0 identically. More explicitly, choose D>max(1,H·max(1,S(Φ))^(q/(q−1))). If E_N≠0 has first nonzero coefficient λ_N, the polynomial Siegel relation gives |λ_N|∞≥D^(−ℓ d q^ℓ), whereas Schwarz–Jensen gives |λ_N|∞≤Mψ H |θ|∞^(−N/(2ℓ)+q/(q−1)), with Mψ=sup_(|z|∞≤|θ|∞)max_i|ψ_i(z)|∞ finite. These inequalities contradict each other for all sufficiently large N.
hypotheses: Write k=F_q(θ), A=F_q[θ], |θ|∞=q, fix a finite separable extension K0/k of degree d, and put K=∪_(ν≥0)K0^(q^(−ν)), O the integral closure of A in K, and O0=O∩K0. All fields are embedded in the chosen k̄⊂C∞.

Fix ℓ>1, Φ∈Mat_ℓ(O[t]) with detΦ=c(t−θ)^s, c∈O nonzero, s≥0; ψ∈E^ℓ satisfies ψ^(−1)=Φψ. Fix 0≠ρ∈O^(1×ℓ) with ρψ(θ)=0, and ϑ∈Mat_(ℓ×(ℓ−1))(O) of rank ℓ−1 with ρϑ=0. Put Θ=adj(Φ), a=1−1/(2ℓ), and δ=deg_t Θ≥0.
proofSteps: The ℓ+1 row vectors h_N, h_N^(−1)Φ, …, h_N^(−ℓ)Φ^(−(ℓ−1))…Φ have size <D. Apply polynomial Siegel to obtain nonzero a_0,…,a_ℓ∈O[t] with Σ a_i E_N^(−i)=0 and max S(a_i)<D^ℓ. Remove their common power of t so at least one a_i(0) is nonzero.

If E_N≠0, its first coefficient λ_N satisfies Σ a_i(0) λ_N^(q^(−i))=0. Raising to q^ℓ gives a nonzero polynomial over O of coefficient size <D^(ℓ q^ℓ). The Liouville inequality and root multiplicity at least one give the stated coarse lower bound.

The N distinct zeros prescribed by the auxiliary constraints lie in |z|≤|θ|. The Schwarz–Jensen factor estimate gives |λ_N||θ|^(N−q/(q−1))≤sup_disk |E_N|. The degree and size bounds on h_N give the stated upper bound.

gaps.title: General rank integrality
gaps.detail: Establish that a non-scalar field Drinfeld action has integral positive proportionality factor deg_τ φ_a/deg_A(a). The displayed valuation proportionality alone gives a rational number. Use the finite projective A_L-module route of Hartl Theorem 3.9, or inspect a full direct integrality proof, without assuming the rank definition as its proof.

gaps.title: Nilpotent-base standardization
gaps.detail: Hartl Lemma 3.8(a), p. 10, cites Drinfeld and Matignon for the unique normalized nonlinear Ore conjugation. Inspect that proof or give the finite nilpotent-induction argument. The current pass establishes the exact statement and its distinction from linear frame change.

gaps.title: Analytic surjectivity and general-A kernel rank
gaps.detail: The BP survey states Theorem 2.1 but does not provide the complete nonarchimedean zero/surjectivity and general-A projective kernel-rank proof. The requested AdicSpaces analytic input and a full uniformization proof must discharge these steps. Finite-subspace products, normalization and the exponential recurrence are specified.

gaps.title: Reciprocal-ring normality proof input

gaps.title: Integral Tate image saturation
gaps.detail: Stalder Proposition 5.16(a), preprint p. 34 and published p. 588, asserts saturation as known. Supply the exact integral argument: λ-divisibility of a realized Hom map descends to divisibility in Hom_A(E,F), using finite-shtuka torsion and the quotient isogeny; retain nonprincipal λ. Rational full faithfulness is proved by the inspected period-ring route.

gaps.title: Drinfeld semisimple-motive input
gaps.detail: Stalder Theorem 1.1 assumes a semisimple A-isomotive. Prove that the rational motive of a field Drinfeld module is simple, or inspect the precise reference supplying it, before deducing unconditional semisimplicity of its point Tate representation.

gaps.title: Elliptic-chain morphism category
gaps.detail: Wiedmann Theorem 5.10 and proof use an equivalence convention with affine-module morphisms. Reconcile it fully with the bounded-shift chain morphisms and the contravariant Hom(E,G_a) convention stated here. The object construction, infinity projectivity/gluing, normalized cohomology and inverse line have been read. At a non-rational infinity point, verify the residue-factor/descent normalization of each length-one quotient in the degree filtration, including how Frobenius permutes the factors, before claiming the unrestricted relative correspondence. The period rδ and the pushforward-to-S line condition are explicit, rather than replacing infinity by a rational leg.

gaps.title: Valued-skew-field proof inputs

Removed unsupported suppliers and kept exact source/implementation inputs as gaps. Confirmed six existing source issues and added four. Complete means a finished planned pass; all eight stages remain planned, none closed. RT-AREA-finitefields/13 has one FF.4 owner. See the report and handoff for reader synchronization and catalogue requests. The coordinate exponential predicates require the infinity-norm hypothesis; period-ring bounded-pole arguments use proper coherent finiteness on projective normal models of any dimension.

importChecks.title: Drinfeld modules
importChecks.statement: Fix a finite field F of size q, a smooth projective geometrically connected curve C/F, a closed point ∞ of degree δ, A=Γ(C−∞,O_C), and an F-algebra field L with characteristic map γ:A→L. A Drinfeld module is an F-algebra map φ:A→L{τ} with ∂φ_a=γ(a), not equal to the scalar map C∘γ. The q-Frobenius Ore ring and its identification with F-linear polynomial group endomorphisms are supplied by FF.4. The characteristic is ker γ; generic characteristic means γ injective. The rank theorem below supplies r rather than imposing a potentially circular definition.
hypotheses: F finite; L field; A as specified, with exact constant field F.
proofSteps: Import the FF.4 composition-ring comparison.
Define the characteristic using the constant-coefficient homomorphism; evaluate on every commutative L-algebra to obtain the group-scheme action.
Use the rank theorem to reconcile this field definition with constant positive rank.
acceptance: C_t=θ+τ has characteristic evaluation at θ.
The action on group-scheme points is natural in the value algebra.

sources.match: The survey gives the differential convention and permits rank zero; the positive-rank non-scalar condition is supplied by Hartl Definition 3.7.
Positive rank excludes the scalar action.

importChecks.title: Rank over the polynomial ring
importChecks.statement: For A=F[t] and φ_t=θ+g_1τ+⋯+g_rτ^r with g_r≠0, r≥1, every nonzero a∈F[t] satisfies deg_τ φ_a=r deg_t a. If d=deg a, its leading coefficient is lc(a)·g_r^(Σ_{i=0}^{d−1}q^(ri)), with empty exponent sum zero.
hypotheses: L field; φ a Drinfeld F[t]-module.
proofSteps: Expand a(φ_t) using the polynomial algebra-map universal property.
FF.4’s Ore multiplication gives the leading coefficient of each power.
The maximal degree term is unique; field nonzero coefficients preclude cancellation.
acceptance: For nonzero constants the degree is zero and leading coefficient is the constant.
For C_t=θ+τ and a=t² the image is θ²+(θ+θ^q)τ+τ².

sources.match: The polynomial-ring rank is the τ-degree of the image of t.

importChecks.title: The general rank theorem
importChecks.statement: For A=Γ(C−∞,O_C) with arbitrary δ=deg∞, a field Drinfeld A-module has a unique integer r≥1 such that deg_τφ_a=r deg_A(a), where deg_A(a)=−δ ord∞(a)=log_q #(A/(a)), for all a≠0. A rational ∞ is not assumed. The assertion includes integrality of r.
hypotheses: The curve and field hypotheses of drinfeld-module.
proofSteps: τ-degree is additive on products and gives an infinity valuation on Frac(A).
Import the function-ring degree and Riemann–Roch facts.

Identify L{τ} with the finite projective A⊗F L motive of the one-dimensional module; its rank supplies the integer r. The final finite-projectivity/integrality input is recorded as a gap rather than inferred from proportional valuations alone.
acceptance: The degree of a depends on δ.
For F[t], recover rank-polynomial-ring.

importChecks.statement: Define rank φ as the unique r supplied by rank-general, normalized by log_q|A/(a)|. Its value is locally constant in relative families; over F[t] it is the nonzero τ-degree of φ_t.
hypotheses: A and L as in drinfeld-module.
proofSteps: Use uniqueness in rank-general to choose r.
Field extension preserves nonzero leading coefficients and hence the degree formula.
acceptance: The invariant is positive and unchanged by field extension.

importChecks.title: The Carlitz module
importChecks.statement: For θ∈L, C:F[t]→L{τ} is the F-algebra map with C_t=θ+τ. Its characteristic is evaluation at θ, rank is one, and C_t acts as x↦θx+x^q. Generic characteristic holds exactly when θ is transcendental over F.
hypotheses: L field containing F.
proofSteps: Apply the polynomial algebra-map universal property to Cθ+τ.

importChecks.title: The characteristic-place realization

importChecks.title: Drinfeld uniformization
importChecks.statement: Every rank-r Drinfeld A-module φ over C_∞ in generic characteristic has a unique entire F-linear exponential exp_φ with derivative one and exp_φ(az)=φ_a(exp_φ(z)). It is surjective; its kernel is a projective A-lattice of rank r. These functors give an equivalence between rank-r field Drinfeld modules over C_∞ and rank-r A-lattices with scalar morphisms. No automatic statement is asserted for arbitrary t-modules or families.
hypotheses: C_∞, generic characteristic, rank r≥1.
proofSteps: For F[t], the coefficient recurrence is α_0=1 and (θ^(q^i)−θ)α_i=Σ_{j=1}^{min(r,i)}g_j α_(i−j)^(q^j).
Establish infinite radius and simple zeros from the analytic input.
The functional equation gives the A-module kernel; quotient torsion counts and the infinite-place finiteness input give projective rank r.
For general A, restrict along a separating F[t]⊂A and recover the full A-action by uniqueness; the exact general-A kernel-rank input is recorded.
acceptance: A nonprincipal ideal lattice stays projective, not artificially free.
The exponential of a general t-module may be nonsurjective.

importChecks.title: Morphisms in uniformization
importChecks.statement: For φ,ψ of the same positive rank r over C_∞, differentiation gives a bijection Hom(φ,ψ)≅{c∈C_∞:cΛ_φ⊂Λ_ψ}; the corresponding polynomial u satisfies u(exp_φ(z))=exp_ψ(cz). It is compatible with A-actions, identities and composition. In particular scalar homothety classifies isomorphisms.
hypotheses: Generic characteristic over C_∞.
The two lattices have the same A-rank r. For c≠0 this makes Λ_ψ/cΛ_φ finite; different-rank scalar inclusions are excluded.
proofSteps: For c≠0 use equal ranks and finite generation to prove the scalar inclusion has finite index; form the corresponding finite F-subspace polynomial. The zero scalar gives the zero morphism separately.
Construct u from the finite quotient when c≠0 and use the normalized product.
Differentiating gives ∂u=c; uniqueness follows from surjectivity.
Use the functional equations to verify intertwining.
acceptance: A nonzero morphism is separable; c=0 corresponds only to u=0.

For A=F[t], take Λ=A and Λ′=A+Aα with α∈F_(q²)∖F⊂C_∞ (so α∉Frac(A)) and the usual infinity embedding. The scalar 1 gives Λ⊂Λ′, but cannot be the differential of a nonzero Ore intertwiner between ranks one and two. This rejects the omitted equal-rank hypothesis.

importChecks.title: The Anderson–Thakur Omega function
importChecks.statement: For the chosen ρ, put Ω(t)=ρ^(−q)∏_{i≥1}(1−t/θ^(q^i)). This product is in the arithmetic entire ring E and is a unit of the radius-one Tate algebra T. It satisfies Ω^(−1)=(t−θ)Ω. Its zeros in C∞ are exactly θ^(q^i), i≥1, each simple. In particular Ω(θ)≠0, Ω is not rational in t, and 1/Ω(θ)=π_N=−π_P, where π_P=θρ∏_{i≥1}(1−θ^(1−q^i))^(−1) is the independently defined numerical period of DM.2. Replacing a weight-w denominator π_P^w by π_N^w multiplies it by (−1)^w.
hypotheses: C∞, k=F_q(θ), k∞ and θ are the normalized embeddings of DM.2; θ is transcendental over F_q, ||θ||=q; choose ρ with ρ^(q−1)=−θ.
proofSteps: Uniform convergence on every disk gives the entire product.
The zero locations lie outside the unit disk; the restricted-series criterion gives a Tate unit.
Shift the product under the inverse coefficient twist and use ρ^(q−1)=−θ.
Evaluate at θ and compare products, retaining the sign.

For coefficient algebraicity and the finite coefficient field, write F(t)=∏(1−t/θ^(q^i)). Then F^(−1)=(1−t/θ)F. Its coefficients b_n satisfy b_n^(1/q)=b_n−b_(n−1)/θ, hence are algebraic over k. All b_n already lie in the complete field k∞ by convergence of finite products; adjoining ρ suffices for Ω. This proves the arithmetic condition beyond entire convergence.
Keep DM.2 free of an analytic Ω prerequisite: its numerical product defines π_P and π_N first; the displayed equality is a later comparison in this layer.
acceptance: Twisting does not replace the variable t by t^q.

Its set of isomorphism classes is not its stack structure.

importChecks.title: Fine level representability and smoothness
importChecks.statement: For any nonzero proper N⊂A, the full level-N functor over Spec A[1/N] is represented by an affine smooth scheme M_r(N) of finite type and relative dimension r−1, with universal family. For a compact open K⊂GL_r(Â), call K fine if its image in some GL_r(A/p) is unipotent. Write N_K for the largest ideal with K(N_K)⊂K. The K-level moduli scheme over A[1/N_K] is a fine smooth moduli scheme when K is fine; for general K it is coarse. These assertions do not require the two-prime condition needed for an all-characteristics level functor over Spec A.
hypotheses: r≥1; A as in DM.0; level primes inverted; K fine for a universal family.
proofSteps: Construct principal-level charts from the standard coefficient and torsion equations.
Infinitesimal deformations give a formally smooth rank-r−1 space; finite presentation supplies smoothness.
Use finite quotients and descent. A scalar fixing a fine level acts both semisimply and unipotently on torsion, hence is one.
The precise chart/deformation proof in Drinfeld §5 is an explicit source proof gap; Hartl–Yu states the result and proves the fine-subgroup extension.

importChecks.title: Generalized Drinfeld modules
importChecks.statement: A generalized Drinfeld A-module of rank ≤r over S is a line bundle E with an F-linear A-action, differential γ, every field fiber a Drinfeld module of positive rank ≤r, and the global degree bound φ_a=Σ_{i=0}^{r deg_A(a)}b_iτ^i. Coefficients b_i are sections of E^(1−q^i). Isomorphisms preserve the line-bundle structure. Weakly separating means that for each algebraically closed field L over the base, any fixed Drinfeld-module isomorphism class occurs at only finitely many points of S(L). The global bound cannot be replaced by a fiberwise bound on nonreduced bases.
hypotheses: S an A-scheme; fixed integer r≥1; standard F-linear line bundle.
proofSteps: Glue the bounded q-linearized coefficient descriptions under line-bundle changes.
Define field-fiber positivity and weak separation independently of level.
Pullback preserves generalized families; weak separation is a condition on the resulting classifying map, not invariant under arbitrary positive-dimensional base change.
acceptance: Boundary rank drops are positive; a scalar action alone is not allowed.

importChecks.title: Drinfeld Hecke correspondences and operators
importChecks.statement: For g∈GL_r(A_f) with entries in Â and compact open K, put K′=K∩g⁻¹Kg. The correspondence is M_r(K)←J_1 M_r(K′)→J_g M_r(K), using quotient isogenies. Its maps extend finitely to the generic Satake compactifications. The induced operator on weight-k forms is T_g=(J_g)_*∘J_1^*, with pullback composed with the isogeny’s Lie-dual identification and pushforward defined by the finite coset trace. It depends only on KgK. For gK′g⁻¹⊂K, (J_g)_*J_g^*=[K:gK′g⁻¹] id; the integer is viewed in characteristic p and may be zero.
hypotheses: Generic-fiber moduli; g integral at every finite place for the specified line normalization; use fine sublevels and invariants if K is not fine.
proofSteps: Construct quotient isogenies from ideal torsion, and identify the Lie line in generic characteristic.
Extend the finite maps and isogenies by Satake uniqueness and generalized-family extension.
Use a common normal fine level and sum translates to define trace; independence follows from subgroup transitivity.
Double-coset convolution follows from the finite correspondence decomposition, without dividing by its degree.
acceptance: A change of level with g=1 has pullback followed by trace equal to its finite index.

importChecks.title: The arithmetic Satake compactification
importChecks.statement: For every fine compact open K⊂GL_r(Â), with N_K the largest ideal satisfying K(N_K)⊂K, M_r(K) over Spec A[1/N_K] has a normal integral projective flat Satake compactification carrying a weakly separating generalized Drinfeld module extending the universal family. Both are unique up to unique compatible isomorphism, and the Lie-dual line is ample. For fine K′⊂K, the level map extends to a finite surjective open map after extending the base to A[1/N_K′], and pulls back the family and Lie-dual line. No flatness of this finite level map or normality/Cohen–Macaulayness of every special fiber is asserted.
hypotheses: r≥1; fine K; excellent Dedekind A; the indicated good open base, not Spec A with level primes retained.
proofSteps: Use the explicit reciprocal model over F[t,1/t] as the seed.
For coefficient restriction, normalize the closure of the fine moduli image in that seed; generalized action maps extend over a normal base.
Take the finite quotient at a principal sublevel; fineness descends the line bundle, normality and weak separation.
Dedekind-base torsion-freeness gives flatness; finite-surjective descent gives ampleness.
Normalized diagonal uniqueness and common-level quotients prove level functoriality.
acceptance: For F[t], level (t), the model is Q_r×Spec F[t,1/t].
Its generic fiber is Pink’s compactification by the defining universal property.

importChecks.title: Anderson t-modules
importChecks.statement: For A=F[t] and an F-algebra field L with γ(t)=θ, a d-dimensional t-module is the F-algebra map Φ:F[t]→Mat_d(L{τ}) acting on G_a^d such that dΦ_t=θI_d+N with N nilpotent. More intrinsically, an Anderson A-module over R is fpqc-locally G_a^d as an F-module scheme and satisfies (dΦ_a−γ(a)I)^d=0 for every a∈A. Morphisms are matrices U with UΦ_a=Ψ_aU. Abelianness means that its contravariant motive is finite locally free over A⊗F R; it is an additional hypothesis.
hypotheses: d≥1 for nontrivial examples; polynomial-ring field coordinate version and relative Anderson version distinguished.
proofSteps: Use FF.4 entrywise to identify F-linear polynomial maps with matrices over the Ore ring.
Use the polynomial algebra-map universal property; the nilpotent differential at t implies the required condition for every a.
Define the matrix intertwiners and their category laws.
Descend the coordinate description to fpqc forms, using SF.1 affine and quasicoherent fpqc descent.
acceptance: Rank-one Drinfeld modules are dimension-one Anderson modules, while motive rank need not equal dimension.

importChecks.title: Effective A-motives
importChecks.statement: Put A_R=A⊗F R, σ=id_A⊗Frob_q,R and J=ker(A_R→R, a⊗b↦γ(a)b). An effective A-motive of rank r and dimension d is a finite projective A_R-module M of rank r with an injective A_R-linear map τ_M:σ* M→M whose cokernel is locally free of rank d over R and annihilated by J^d. Without specifying dimension, Hartl calls a motive effective when some J^n kills the cokernel; this weaker condition alone does not define dimension d over a nonreduced base. Here σ*M=M⊗_(A_R,σ) A_R. Morphisms are A_R-linear maps commuting with this linearized Frobenius. For polynomial A over a field, coker dimension is d and (t−θ)^n kills it for some n; d also bounds a nilpotence exponent. No perfection of R is required.
hypotheses: A as in DM.0; commutative F-algebra R and characteristic map γ; locally constant r,d.
proofSteps: Define scalar extension along σ with native tensor products and its linearized map.
Form the module cokernel and support at J.
Over nonreduced or imperfect coefficients use linearization, not the raw semilinear image; scalar extension is essential.

Retain J^d coker τ_M=0 in the dimension-d structure. Over a field the dimension bound follows from nilpotence on a d-dimensional vector space; that argument does not extend to an arbitrary nonreduced R.
acceptance: The Frobenius fixes A and raises only coefficient-ring elements to q-th powers.

importChecks.title: The contravariant motive functor
importChecks.statement: For an Anderson A-module E/R, set M(E)=Hom_(F-module schemes/R)(E,G_a,R). A acts by precomposition with φ_a and R acts by postcomposition with scalars; τ acts by postcomposition with q-Frobenius. When E is coordinate G_a^d this is the row module R{τ}^{1×d}. For a morphism f:E→E′, M(f):M(E′)→M(E) is precomposition by f. If E is abelian of rank r and dimension d, this is an effective A-motive and coker τ_M≅Hom_R(Lie E,R).

proofSteps: Entrywise FF.4 gives the row representation.
The A-action is right composition with φ_a and commutes with left τ and R.

Finite projectivity and support at J follow from abelianness and the nilpotent differential.

importChecks.title: The abelian Anderson anti-equivalence
importChecks.statement: The contravariant functor E↦M(E) is fully faithful from abelian Anderson A-modules over R to effective A-motives. Its essential image consists exactly of effective motives that become finite free left R′{τ}-modules after a faithfully flat coefficient extension R→R′. Rank over A_R is the Anderson rank, and coker τ_M has R-rank equal to the group dimension. For polynomial A over a field, the corresponding category is effective L[t]-motives finite free over L{τ}; this is not the category of all effective A-motives.
hypotheses: Same coefficient algebra and characteristic; abelianness and fpqc-local Ore freeness; no generic-characteristic assumption in the relative theorem.
proofSteps: Choose an Ore basis after faithfully flat extension.
Right matrices for the A-action reconstruct φ; the cokernel condition gives its nilpotent differential.
Intertwiner matrices identify Hom in the reversed direction.
Use effective fpqc descent of affine groups and morphisms to descend the reconstructed object.
acceptance: The n-th Carlitz tensor motive reconstructs an n-dimensional t-module.
A general effective motive without local Ore freeness is not assigned an Anderson module.

sources.match: The theorem gives full faithfulness and the precise fpqc-local Ore-free essential image.

importChecks.title: Purity of polynomial-ring motives
importChecks.statement: For an abelian t-motive M of rank r over L[t], extend it to L((1/t)). It is pure if there are positive integers u,v and an L[[1/t]]-lattice H of rank r such that t^uH=τ^vH, interpreted via v-fold linearized coefficient Frobenius. The weight is u/v, independent of this choice, and equals d/r for a nonzero pure effective motive of dimension d. Purity is additional data/property, not part of the definition of every t-module or every effective motive.
hypotheses: Polynomial A; pure effective finite-rank motive; the positive-dimension weight statement is in this range.
The raw Frobenius-image lattice formulation in the Suggested coordinate model uses perfect L; over imperfect coefficients use the linearized scalar-pullback formulation, not an unlinearized image.
proofSteps: Specify the infinity lattice and iterate of the linearized map.
Compare determinants of τ^v on the lattice to identify u/v=d/r.
A common iterate compares two choices and proves weight independence.
acceptance: Carlitz tensor power n has weight n, not 1/n.

sources.match: Purity uses a Frobenius-stable infinity lattice and fixes the rank/dimension weight convention.
Weight is d/r and agrees with u/v for every purity-lattice witness; raw Frobenius is used over perfect coefficients.

importChecks.title: Uniformizable t-modules
importChecks.statement: For an abelian t-module E over C_∞ with differential θI+N, its unique normalized entire exponential exp_E:C_∞^d→E(C_∞) intertwines dΦ_t with Φ_t. Uniformizable means this map is surjective. Its kernel Λ_E is discrete and carries the differential A-action. Export this predicate and the exponential to DM.8, whose rigid-triviality comparison identifies it with analytic triviality under the abelian hypotheses. The rigid predicate and its comparison are owned by DM.8; they are not prerequisites for defining exp_E or uniformizability here.
hypotheses: C_∞; abelian t-module, generic characteristic, exact analytic hypotheses of the selected theorem.
In the normed coordinate prototype, 1<‖θ‖ is an argument of the exponential and the predicates themselves; no arbitrary special-characteristic exponential is posited.
proofSteps: Solve the matrix coefficient recurrence; the nilpotent differential gives unique coefficients and infinite radius.
Form the kernel and the surjectivity predicate using the actual exponential map.

Export the normalized exponential, its kernel and the surjectivity predicate to the DM.8 rigid-triviality comparison; its proof is the consumer’s responsibility. No circular prerequisite on that comparison is introduced.

importChecks.title: Effective dual t-motives
importChecks.statement: Over a perfect coefficient field L containing F, let L[t,σ] have σc=c^(1/q)σ and σt=tσ. An effective dual t-motive is a finite free L[t]-module H with inverse-q-semilinear σ and (t−θ)^ℓ(H/σH)=0 for some ℓ≥0; the image here is an L[t]-submodule because L is perfect. In the finite-dimensional t-module correspondence also require H finite free over L[σ], of rank d; call that condition A-finiteness on the dual side. These two versions are distinguished explicitly. The Ngo Dac source uses the first, broader effective definition.
hypotheses: L perfect; generic θ in period applications; the L[σ]-freeness condition is not silently added to Ngo Dac Definition 4.1.
proofSteps: Import inverse coefficient twisting from DM.8.
Define the Ore module with variable t fixed by the twist.
Use its σ-cokernel to express characteristic support; maintain the stronger Ore-freeness eligibility as a separate condition.
Use inverse iterateFrobeniusEquiv on the perfect algebraic coefficient field, extended to polynomial coefficients. No Tate algebra, arithmetic entire ring or analytic coefficient twist is needed.

An intertwiner U:Φ→Ψ induces h↦hU* from the row module for Φ to that for Ψ, so this dual construction is covariant. Finite freeness over L[t] is a separate A-finiteness hypothesis.

importChecks.title: Dual motives and t-module points
importChecks.statement: For the row dual module H=L[σ]^{1×d} associated to Φ over a perfect field, define δ₁(Σ h_iσ^i)=Σ h_i^(q^i) coordinatewise. It induces an F-linear A-module isomorphism H/(σ−1)H≅E(L), with the t-action inherited from Φ_t*. The denominator means the F-linear image of σ−1, not an L-linear submodule. For an effective dual motive finite free over both L[t] and L[σ], this reconstructs its A-finite t-module; over perfect L this is abelian as well: Maurischat Theorem 6.6 proves abelian iff A-finite, and Corollary 8.1 extends this equivalence to Anderson A-modules by restriction along a finite extension A/F[t]. This theorem concerns finite generation of the motive of an actual Anderson module; it does not add Ore-finiteness to the broader effective dual-motive definition.
hypotheses: Perfect L; finite Ore rank d; use A-finiteness for a finite L[t]-rank dual motive.
proofSteps: Reduce σ-degree using (σ−1) and inverse coefficient twist.
δ₁ is zero on this image and each row has a unique constant representative in the quotient.
The star relation identifies the t-action with the original coordinate action.

For a matrix D defining Φ_t, use the left and right block-power rank criteria of Propositions 6.4 and 6.5. Theorem 4.1 identifies both criteria with positive slopes of the last invariant factor of tI−D over the complete valued skew field L({σ}); Proposition 6.1 turns either criterion into both finite-generation conclusions. This Laurent σ=τ⁻¹ convention is distinct from the literal star dual module.

For general A choose a nonconstant t by Riemann–Roch; A is finite over F[t], so finite generation over A⊗F L is equivalent to finite generation over L[t]. Retain perfect coefficients; no relative nonperfect-base theorem is asserted.

importChecks.title: Rational motives and their Tate realization
importChecks.statement: Let K_0=Frac(A) and L a coefficient field with fixed γ. Rationalize the effective A-motive category by Hom⁰(M,N)=K_0⊗A Hom(M,N). For λ≠ker γ put L_(λ)=the total quotient ring Frac((F_λ⊗F L)[[z]]) after a residue-field splitting, where F_λ=A/λ and z is a local parameter. Complete M to this coefficient ring and take τ-invariants after L→L^sep; this gives its rational Tate realization V_λ(M) over K_0,λ. For a Drinfeld module E, V_λ(E) is canonically dual to V_λ(M(E)); the dual changes the motive’s Hom direction back to the group’s direction. The precise finite-level pairing is supplied by the finite-shtuka realization.
hypotheses: Effective finite-rank motives with characteristic λ avoided; splitting factors are retained, not discarded.

Frac for the split completed coefficient algebra denotes its total quotient ring, with every residue-field factor retained; it is generally a product of fields. The rational scalar extension K_0,λ,L=Frac(K_0,λ⊗F L) is not replaced by the full Laurent-series completion.
proofSteps: Localize Hom at nonzero elements of A and prove well-defined composition.
Complete the module and its linearized Frobenius; it is invertible at λ.
Use finite-shtuka pairing and passage to inverse limits for the dual identification.

importChecks.title: Injectivity of the Tate comparison
importChecks.statement: The natural integral Tate comparison α_λ is injective for field Drinfeld modules with λ away from characteristic. In particular a morphism acting as zero on every λ-power torsion scheme is zero. The tensor statement uses finite torsion-freeness of the Hom A-module, not only pointwise injectivity of u↦T_λu.
hypotheses: The field, characteristic and prime hypotheses of tate-hom-map.
proofSteps: A nonzero q-polynomial cannot kill torsion of unbounded scheme order.

If a completion-linear combination acts trivially, reduce modulo λ^n and use λ-divisibility of Hom: vanishing on E[λ^n] implies factorization through the ideal isogeny. This integral division input is recorded with tate-image-saturation.

importChecks.title: Local algebraization of motive maps
importChecks.statement: Let L be finitely generated over F. Put K_0,L=Frac(K_0⊗F L), K_0,λ,L=Frac(K_0,λ⊗F L), and L_(λ)=Frac((F_λ⊗F L)[[z]]). A restricted module means a finite projective module with invertible Frobenius linearization; at λ it has a finite-projective integral lattice with invertible Frobenius. Extension K_0,L→K_0,λ,L is K_0,λ/K_0-fully faithful on such modules and preserves semisimple objects. Extension K_0,λ,L→L_(λ) is fully faithful on the λ-restricted objects and preserves semisimple objects. Thus completed Frobenius-equivariant maps are algebraized over the rational coefficient ring. The first ring is not the full completed Laurent-series ring unless L is finite.
hypotheses: Finitely generated coefficient field L, hence finitely many roots of unity; K_0,λ/K_0 separable; the λ-restricted integral model condition is explicit.

Frac for the split completed coefficient algebra denotes its total quotient ring, with every residue-field factor retained; it is generally a product of fields. The rational scalar extension K_0,λ,L=Frac(K_0,λ⊗F L) is not replaced by the full Laurent-series completion.
proofSteps: For scalar extension, reduce to finite and one-variable transcendental extensions; Frobenius-fixed denominators descend to the constant field.
Prove separability of the function-field completion by a separating local parameter.
Use the period ring and its two fixed-ring identities to construct a full faithful left-adjoint realization functor.
Every invariant subobject is quasigeometric; the descended lattice supplies the λ-restricted condition.
acceptance: When L is finite the two local coefficient rings agree; for positive transcendence degree they need not.

sources.locator: Theorem 3.11 with proof, pp. 18–21; Theorem 4.8 and Proposition 4.9, pp. 25–26; Theorem 5.15, p. 33

importChecks.title: The Tate period ring
importChecks.statement: For finitely generated L/F choose a projective normal F-model X of its function field and compatible extensions of each prime-divisor valuation to L^sep. Inside L_(λ)^sep, let B⁺ be the Laurent series whose coefficients have valuation bounded below at every compatible prime divisor and are integral outside a finite set of divisors of X. Let S consist of invertible integral local series s with σ(s)/s∈K_0,λ⊗F L. Set B=B⁺[S⁻¹]. It has B^σ=K_0,λ and B^G_L=K_0,λ,L, contains every τ-fixed solution of a λ-restricted finite-rank system, and yields B⊗_(K_0,λ) V_λ(M)≅B⊗_(K_0,λ,L)M. Full completion cannot replace B in the algebraization argument.
hypotheses: L finitely generated over F; normal proper model; valuation extensions normalized by ramification; finite residue factors retained; σ is q-coefficient Frobenius fixing z.

Frac for the split completed coefficient algebra denotes its total quotient ring, with every residue-field factor retained; it is generally a product of fields. The rational scalar extension K_0,λ,L=Frac(K_0,λ⊗F L) is not replaced by the full Laurent-series completion.

Projective normal finite-type F-models exist by projective closure and finite normalization. Transcendence degree need not be one; bounded-pole section spaces use proper coherent finiteness in any dimension.
proofSteps: Choose a projective normal F-model, of any transcendence degree. Cover the finitely many exceptional prime-divisor supports by an effective Cartier divisor using a nonzero homogeneous section of a projective embedding, and raise its power to bound the coefficient poles. The coefficients then lie in H^0(X,O_X(nD)), finite-dimensional by proper coherent finiteness (SF.2/ample-serre-vanishing with a chosen ample line). A curve-only Riemann–Roch statement is not used for higher-dimensional models.
Construct integral Frobenius units and invert them; the formal functional equations move all solutions into B.
Prove the σ-fixed and Galois-fixed ring identities before applying invariant tensor arguments.
The semilinear fixed-vector basis gives the comparison isomorphism. The construction and properties are proved in Stalder §6, not posited as fields in a structure.
acceptance: The Galois-fixed ring is the rational coefficient ring K_0,λ,L, not the larger completed ring L_(λ).

importChecks.title: Integral Hom division and saturation
importChecks.statement: For E,E′ over the same coefficient field and λ away from characteristic, the image of A_λ⊗A Hom_L(E,E′) in Hom_(A_λ,G_L)(T_λE,T_λE′) is saturated. Equivalently, if z·h is in the image for a local uniformizer z and h is an integral equivariant Tate map, then h is in the image. Prove this by finite-level kernel factorization/divisibility of algebraic intertwiners, using descent of the quotient isogeny. Rational surjectivity alone does not prove this assertion.
hypotheses: Same characteristic; prime-to-characteristic torsion; finite-projective Hom; local uniformizer chosen only in the completed DVR.
proofSteps: If a morphism kills a finite ideal-torsion subgroup, factor it through the corresponding quotient Drinfeld module.
Translate divisibility in the completed Hom lattice to the corresponding λ-adic torsion kernels, without assuming λ principal in A.

importChecks.title: The Drinfeld Tate theorem
importChecks.statement: Let L be finitely generated over F, let E,E′ be Drinfeld A-modules over the same (L,γ), and let λ≠ker γ. The comparison α_λ:A_λ⊗A Hom_L(E,E′)→Hom_(A_λ,G_L)(T_λE,T_λE′) is an isomorphism. Inverting λ yields the rational version. The theorem allows both generic and special characteristic; it does not permit different characteristic maps, an algebraically closed infinite coefficient field in place of a finitely generated one, or λ equal to the characteristic.
hypotheses: Exact fixed-characteristic and finitely generated coefficient-field hypotheses.
proofSteps: Pass contravariantly to effective motives and dualize their Tate realizations.
Apply local-algebraization to the rational motive Hom category, whose embedding is fully faithful after coefficient localization.
Combine rational bijectivity with integral injectivity and tate-image-saturation.
The integral last step remains a named proof input; neither the rational theorem nor Tamagawa’s earlier sketch supplies it by itself.

importChecks.title: Semisimplicity of rational Tate representations
importChecks.statement: For finitely generated L/F and λ away from characteristic, the rational Tate realization of a semisimple A-isomotive is a semisimple K_0,λ-representation of G_L. In particular the rational Tate representation of every Drinfeld module is semisimple. The latter uses the separate fact that a Drinfeld motive is simple in the rational motive category; a general effective Anderson motive is not assumed semisimple.
hypotheses: Finitely generated L; fixed characteristic avoided by λ; motive semisimplicity for the general version.
proofSteps: The rational motive category embeds faithfully in restricted Frobenius modules and preserves semisimplicity.
Each of the two local scalar extensions preserves semisimple objects by local-algebraization.
The local Frobenius/Galois equivalence transfers semisimplicity to the representation.

The Drinfeld-motive simplicity proof, derived from its Ore-module rank-one presentation and degree, is a precise remaining source input. Duality preserves the semisimplicity of the Drinfeld point realization.

This is a polynomial, not the integer cardinality. It is multiplicative in short exact sequences; |0|=1 and #M=q^(deg |M|). The variable T is kept distinct from the coefficient θ used in the integral model.

importChecks.title: Taelman integral Drinfeld models
importChecks.statement: Fix A=F[t], a finite field extension K/F(θ), R the integral closure of F[θ] in K, and γ(t)=θ. An integral model is E_t=θ+r_1τ+⋯+r_nτ^n with r_i∈R and r_n≠0. importChecks.title: Finite-field nuclear determinants
importChecks.statement: Let V be a compact topological F-vector space. A continuous F-linear endomorphism is locally contracting if on some open invariant subspace U its norm decreases by a constant c<1. For Φ=Σ_(n≥1)φ_nZ^n with locally contracting coefficients define det_(F[[Z]])(1+Φ|V) modulo Z^N using a common contracting nucleus for φ₁,…,φ_(N−1) and the determinant on the finite quotient V/U; the compatible residues define the series. It is independent of the common nuclei for the fixed norm. Exact-sequence multiplicativity holds. For continuous endomorphisms a,b, Taelman’s cyclic theorem gives det(1−abZ)=det(1−baZ) when a, ab and ba are all locally contracting; the plus-sign variant follows by replacing a by −a. No arbitrary-series cyclic theorem or unrestricted norm-invariance assertion is made. This finite-field compact-vector-space theory differs from the complex Banach nuclear-operator theory already owned by OperatorTheory.
hypotheses: F finite; compact V; continuous endomorphisms; norm/topology chosen as in Taelman §2; each coefficient locally contracting and no constant coefficient.
The compact F-vector space is normed, with its nonarchimedean norm inducing the topology and the trivial norm on F. Local contraction is measured in this norm.
proofSteps: Every finite coefficient list admits a common nucleus.
On a smaller common nucleus, the contracting piece contributes determinant one modulo the required power of Z.
Finite-dimensional determinant identities descend to the inverse limit of truncations.
Prove invariance under equivalent compact norms and functorial conjugation.

For the cyclic law apply Taelman Theorem 2 with its three contraction assumptions. Its proof chooses common nuclei and bounds the intermediate images; nuclearity of the two products alone is not the cited hypothesis.
acceptance: For finite-dimensional V, recover the ordinary determinant.

sources.locator: Definitions 3–5 and Propositions 6–10, pp. 377–379; Theorem 2, p. 380
sources.match: Nuclearity is coefficientwise local contraction and the determinant is a compatible finite-quotient limit.

uses.how: Trace formula and infinitely tangent comparison determinants.

importChecks.title: The finite-field trace formula
importChecks.statement: For R and K_∞ in the integral-model setting, a finite projective R-module M with q-Frobenius-semilinear τ_M, and Θ∈R{τ}[[Z]]·τZ acting through τ_M, the product over maximal ideals satisfies ∏_m det(1+Θ|M/mM)=det(1+Θ|(M⊗R K_∞)/M)⁻¹. The right-hand coefficients are nuclear. Both sides converge in F[[Z]]. The Frobenius-divisibility condition on Θ is essential; scalar multiplication alone is not this trace formula.
hypotheses: Finite projective M over R; τ_M semilinear with respect to r↦r^q; Θ has no Z⁰ or τ⁰ term.
proofSteps: Prove local contraction for positive-Frobenius operators on the compact quotient.
Use localization exact sequences to isolate finite primes.
Apply Anderson’s commutator factorization to reduce arbitrary nuclear Θ to finite local factors.
Use determinant exactness/cyclic invariance to pass to the Euler product.
acceptance: Specializing Θ=(1−E_tT⁻¹)/(1−θT⁻¹)−1 gives the L-value determinant, after taking the inverse of each local factor.

sources.locator: §3 setup, pp. 381–382; Theorem 3 and proof, pp. 382–384
sources.match: The formula applies to positive-Frobenius series on finite projective modules, with the inverse on the compact quotient.

importChecks.title: Infinitely tangent comparison maps
importChecks.statement: For lattices Λ_i⊂V and finite A-modules H_i put M_i=(V/Λ_i)×H_i. A continuous F-linear map γ:M₁→M₂ is N-tangent to the identity on V if, on some open U⊂V avoiding both lattices, its V/Λ₂ component restricts to an isometry and its local lift obeys ‖γ(v)−v‖≤‖θ^(−N)‖‖v‖. It is infinitely tangent if this holds for every N≥1, with U allowed to vary. For a continuous F-linear isomorphism γ define Δ_γ=Σ_(n≥1)(θ−γ⁻¹tγ)θ^(n−1)T^(−n) on M₁, where θ denotes the source t-action in this operator formula.
hypotheses: Finite-dimensional local V, full lattices, finite H_i; local comparison in quotient charts; γ need not be A-linear.
proofSteps: Define the local lifts after avoiding lattice translates and require the isometry explicitly.
The differential-one entire exponential is infinitely tangent by shrinking its inverse-function neighborhood for each N.
Transport t-actions across γ to obtain the operator series.
acceptance: Infinitely tangent maps can compare distinct t-actions and need not be module homomorphisms.

sources.locator: Definitions 6–7, Proposition 12 and the definition of Δ_γ, pp. 385–386
sources.match: The norm estimate alone is not the whole condition: an isometry on a common open chart is required.

importChecks.title: The tangent determinant identity
importChecks.statement: For a continuous F-linear isomorphism γ:(V/Λ₁)×H₁→(V/Λ₂)×H₂ infinitely tangent to the identity on V, the series Δ_γ is nuclear and det(1+Δ_γ|M₁)=[Λ₁:Λ₂]·|H₂|/|H₁|. This fixes the covolume orientation and the class numerator. No determinant of an arbitrary infinite-dimensional automorphism is used.
hypotheses: The tangent-comparison hypotheses; γ an isomorphism; H_i finite A-modules.
proofSteps: Compute when Λ_i have a common over-lattice and the comparison is an admissible local identity.
Approximate an arbitrary lattice by one sharing such an over-lattice, modulo a prescribed T-adic precision.
N-tangency makes the nuclear determinant unchanged to that precision; pass through all precisions.
acceptance: An identity comparison with equal lattices and finite modules yields determinant one.

sources.match: The identity gives [Λ₁:Λ₂]|H₂|/|H₁|, with no hidden degree normalization.

importChecks.title: Taelman’s class formula
importChecks.statement: For every Taelman integral model E/R, including nonunit leading coefficient and rank zero, L(E/R)=[R:U(E/R)]·|H(E/R)| in F((T⁻¹)). All local factors are those of the chosen integral model. The formula is not generalized here to arbitrary A, arbitrary higher-dimensional t-motives, or complex L-values.
hypotheses: Exactly integral-model; exponential, lattice and monic-cardinality normalizations fixed above.
proofSteps: The trace formula identifies L with det(1+Θ|K_∞/R), Θ=(1−E_tT⁻¹)/(1−θT⁻¹)−1.
The exponential gives 0→K_∞/U→E(K_∞)/E(R)→H→0.
Split the finite quotient continuously as an F-vector space; compare to (K_∞/U)×H by an infinitely tangent isomorphism.
Apply tangent-determinant with Λ₁=R, Λ₂=U, H₁=0, H₂=H.
acceptance: For Carlitz recover ζ_A(1)=log_C(1).
For E_t=θ+θ³τ over F₂[θ], retain |H|=T and recover L=ι(π/θ²).

sources.match: The theorem treats the chosen integral model and keeps its finite class module.

importChecks.title: Depth-one Carlitz power sums
importChecks.statement: For A=F[θ] let A_(d,+) be its finite set of monic degree-d polynomials and S_d(s)=Σ_(a∈A_(d,+))a^(−s). For d≥0 and 1≤s≤q, S_d(s)=ℓ_d^(−s) with ℓ_d=∏_(i=1)^d(θ−θ^(q^i)). Frobenius gives S_d(ps)=S_d(s)^p for p=char F. In particular ζ_A(1)=Σ_dℓ_d⁻¹=log_C(1). The formula ℓ_d^(−s) is not asserted for every s.
hypotheses: Integer s≥1; θ transcendental; the small-exponent formula requires s≤q.
proofSteps: The Carlitz generating product/partial fraction identity computes the small-degree coefficient.
Use the product denominators from DM.0, retaining their sign.
Apply characteristic-p Frobenius to extend along p-power exponents, while keeping its exact range.
The d-sum converges in K_∞ and matches the Carlitz logarithm at one.
acceptance: For q=2,d=1,s=3, S₁(3)=(θ²+θ+1)/(θ(θ+1))³ differs from ℓ₁⁻³.
For d=0, the only monic constant is one, so S₀(s)=1.

sources.match: The depth-one generating identity gives the small-exponent specialization; its range is retained.

importChecks.title: Carlitz and a nonzero class module
importChecks.statement: For Carlitz over F[θ], H=0, U=A log_C(1), and L(C/A)=ζ_A(1)=log_C(1), after renaming θ as T. For q=2, define E_t=θ+θ³τ over F₂[θ]. Then exp_E(x)=θ⁻³exp_C(θ³x), U_E=(π/θ³)A, H_E≅F₂[t]/(t), and L(E/A)=ι(π/θ²). The class is represented by θ⁻¹ and t annihilates it. Thus |H_E|=T is indispensable.
hypotheses: First example the Carlitz integral model; second q=2, K=F₂(θ), R=F₂[θ], π the DM.2 period lying in K_∞ in this case.
proofSteps: At q=2, ‖π‖=4 and π∈K_∞. Reduce any x modulo πA to degree ≤1 by cancelling leading terms.
On the degree-≤1 ball, exp_C is an isometric bijection: higher terms are strictly smaller, and the complete-field contraction argument gives its inverse. Hence exp_C(K_∞)=θF₂[[θ⁻¹]].
Scalar conjugation by θ³ yields exp_E(K_∞)=θ⁻²F₂[[θ⁻¹]]. Its intersection with A is zero, and the quotient modulo A has the single basis class θ⁻¹.
E_t(θ⁻¹)=1+θ lies in A, proving H_E≅A/(t); the unit lattice is θ⁻³ker exp_C.

Away from (θ), the reduction is conjugate to Carlitz; at (θ), its local factor is one. Thus L(E/A)=ζ_A(1)(T−1)/T=ι(π/θ²), also matching regulator times T. The period relation at q=2 is π=(θ²+θ)log_C(1), obtained from the Carlitz torsion equation and the monic product normalization.
acceptance: Dropping the class term in the second example gives a Laurent series with leading term T⁻¹ instead of the Euler product’s leading term one.

sources.locator: Example 3, p. 373; Definition 2 and Remark 2, p. 371
sources.match: The first case is stated in the paper. The scaled q=2 example is derived here from these definitions and the sourced Carlitz period, with every calculation shown; it is not attributed as a source example.

importChecks.title: Elliptic sheaves on the global curve
importChecks.statement: On C×F S put σ=id_C×Frob_q,S. A rank-r elliptic sheaf consists of vector bundles E_i, i∈Z, and injections j_i:E_i→E_(i+1), τ_i:σ*E_i→E_(i+1), satisfying j_(i+1)τ_i=τ_(i+1)σ*j_i and a compatible periodicity E_(i+rδ)≅E_i(∞). Each j_i cokernel is supported on ∞×S and its pushforward to S is a line bundle; each τ_i cokernel is supported on the graph of the characteristic c:S→C−∞ and its pushforward is a line bundle. Maps are bounded-shift compatible chain maps E_i→E′_(i+n), with n≥0 independent of i, identified under further j-shifts. For the Drinfeld correspondence use the normalized/transverse subcategory below. These are bundles on the original global curve C.
hypotheses: C smooth projective geometrically connected over F; ∞ closed of degree δ; r≥1; characteristic leg disjoint from ∞; coherent injections and finite-flat length-one cokernels as specified.
proofSteps: Import native coherent locally free sheaves and effective divisor twists from the existing AlgebraicVectorBundles and AlgebraicCurves roadmaps via SF.0.
Build the integer-indexed periodic diagram with the Frobenius pullback and its commutative squares.
Define bounded-shift morphisms and compose by adding shifts; fixed-index maps alone miss nonconstant Drinfeld isogenies.
acceptance: For rational ∞ and rank one, E_(i+1)=E_i(∞); for rank two, E_(i+2)=E_i(∞).

sources.locator: Definition 5.1, p. 72; Propositions 5.5 and Lemma 5.7, pp. 73–74; §5.4, pp. 80–84
sources.match: The diagram, r·deg∞ periodicity and quotient line conditions are explicit; the normalized transversality identifies the characteristic support.

importChecks.title: Normalized elliptic sheaves
importChecks.statement: The normalized Drinfeld subcategory consists of elliptic sheaves with χ(E_(−1),s)=0 on every field fiber and with τ_i inducing isomorphisms σ*(E_i/E_(i−1))≅E_(i+1)/E_i. Equivalently, the images of E_i and σ*E_i span E_(i+1) and intersect in σ*E_(i−1). In this subcategory, H⁰(E_(−1),s)=H¹(E_(−1),s)=0; for i≥0, H¹(E_i,s)=0 and dim H⁰(E_i,s)=i+1. Thus pr_S*E_0 is a line bundle and the normalized degree is deg E_(−1)=r(g−1).
hypotheses: Same disjoint characteristic leg; exact scalar-field/Frobenius pullback; fiberwise Euler characteristic and the transverse diagram condition.
proofSteps: Use the exact transverse square to obtain 0→σ*E_(i−1)→E_i⊕σ*E_i→E_(i+1)→0.
Apply fiberwise Riemann–Roch and the first nonzero section argument to locate index zero.
Import cohomology and base change to produce the pushforward line and the finite-step sections.
acceptance: Normalization fixes an index and cannot be dropped without changing the moduli category.

importChecks.title: The elliptic sheaf of a Drinfeld module
importChecks.statement: For a standard relative rank-r Drinfeld A-module E on S, its contravariant motive M is finite locally free of rank r over A⊗F O_S and locally free of rank one over O_S{τ}. Filter a local Ore presentation by τ-degree. On a local coefficient algebra R, inside M⊗A K define the infinity lattice E_(i,∞) by deg_τ(m⊗a)=deg_τ(m)−rδ ord∞(a)≤i. Glue this with the motive on (C−∞)×S to obtain E_i. Inclusion gives j_i, left τ gives σ*E_i→E_(i+1), and multiplication by a local inverse uniformizer gives E_(i+rδ)=E_i(∞). These bundles form a normalized elliptic sheaf.
hypotheses: Relative standard rank r, general A and ∞; the gluing is on the original global curve, with fpqc/Zariski coordinate descent.
proofSteps: Finite generators for the infinity-degree filtration and its successive quotient line prove finite presentation.
Prove projectivity over R⊗O_(C,∞), using field fibers, the nilpotent-base flatness argument and finite coefficient descent.
Glue the finite projective modules across the punctured infinity neighborhood using the existing vector-bundle patching interface.
Check the characteristic quotient and transverse squares; sections recover the τ-degree filtration and the normalized cohomology.
Coordinate changes act contravariantly on the motive; a degree-n intertwiner shifts the filtration by at most n.
acceptance: The construction’s affine restriction is M(E), not a new free rank-r τ-module.

sources.match: The infinity filtration, projectivity, gluing and arbitrary-base line-bundle version are spelled out.

importChecks.title: The normalized elliptic-sheaf dictionary
importChecks.statement: The contravariant filtered-motive construction gives an anti-equivalence between standard relative Drinfeld A-modules of rank r and normalized transverse elliptic sheaves of rank r with bounded-shift morphisms. The inverse uses the line (pr_S*E_0)∨ and the Ore module Γ((C−∞)×S,E_0), locally free of rank one over O_S{τ}; right A-action reconstructs the Drinfeld map. Equivalently, this is a covariant equivalence with the opposite elliptic-sheaf category; no self-duality identification of that category is asserted. Characteristic and rank are preserved, and good-open level structures transport through the finite-shtuka pairing.
hypotheses: The normalized/transverse/disjoint-leg conditions and morphism convention above; standard relative Drinfeld objects.
proofSteps: Use the normalized cohomology to identify the generator line and its Frobenius iterates.
The affine sections form the Ore module; multiplication by a∈A respects the filtration and has unit leading term.
Construct the inverse action locally and descend the line-bundle maps.
The two constructions recover the same filtered module; evaluate the morphism maps to verify reversed composition and natural inverse isomorphisms.
acceptance: The generator of sections is dual to the point-line generator, as in the motive functor.

sources.locator: Theorem 5.10 and proof, pp. 75–84; Proposition 5.21, pp. 78–79; §5.4.2, pp. 82–84
sources.match: The source calls the categories equivalent; the contravariant Hom-to-G_a convention fixes the opposite category here. Bounded-shift morphism reconciliation is an explicit source gap.

importChecks.title: The two-leg global shtuka export
importChecks.statement: From the elliptic chain take E_0 and α=j_0⁻¹τ_0:σ*E_0|_U≅E_0|_U, where U=(C×S)−((∞×S)∪Γ_c). The τ- and j-cokernels provide the characteristic zero and infinity pole bounds of a GL_r-modification. At rational ∞ they are length-one modifications; at general δ the pole support and residue factors are retained as the specified infinity chain rather than replaced by a rational leg. Export this datum to the independently defined global G-shtuka category in GS.2. The global category does not supply elliptic sheaves back to this construction.
hypotheses: Normalized elliptic sheaf, characteristic disjoint from infinity; use its actual bound and coefficient ring.
proofSteps: Restrict where both injections are isomorphisms and compose in the stated Frobenius direction.
Pass from the rank-r vector bundle to its GL_r frame torsor using existing vector-bundle APIs.
Record the two modifications with their cokernels and preserve levels by restriction.
GS.2 consumes the resulting datum; no dependency on its elliptic-sheaf-realisation node is introduced.
acceptance: The Frobenius acts on S, leaving the global curve fixed.

sources.match: The two injections and their disjoint quotient supports give the rational Frobenius modification.

importChecks.title: Prime-to-characteristic realization comparison
importChecks.statement: For a normalized elliptic sheaf attached to E and λ away from the characteristic, complete its affine motive M at λ. Its τ-fixed completed realization is canonically dual to T_λE, with the A_λ-linear Galois pairing obtained at each λ^n level from the finite-shtuka functor. The pairing is compatible with all Drinfeld morphisms, bounded shifts of elliptic-chain maps, base extension and prime-to-characteristic level frames.
hypotheses: Field coefficient L for Galois realization, λ away from ker γ; full completed residue factors; contravariant motive convention.
proofSteps: Reduce M modulo λ^n and apply the strict finite-shtuka/group-scheme anti-equivalence.
Identify the torsion points with the dual Frobenius-fixed module by the evaluation pairing.
Pass through the chosen division coordinates to the Tate limit and duality.
acceptance: For Carlitz the point Tate character and the motive-fixed character are inverse, as required by the pairing.

sources.locator: Definition 6.1, p. 23; Theorem 6.4, pp. 24–26; Proposition 6.5 and Theorem 6.6, p. 26
sources.match: Finite-shtuka torsion realizes the motive reductions; inverse limits give the prime-to-characteristic comparison.

importChecks.title: The effective characteristic local comparison
importChecks.statement: For characteristic p and an F_p-algebra R with nilpotent uniformizer image γ(z), completing the affine motive of the elliptic sheaf and selecting the characteristic residue factor gives the same rank-r effective local shtuka as DM.1, with q^(deg p)-Frobenius and the dimension-one cokernel bound. Its finite reductions correspond to the full p-power strict finite group schemes. This is a comparison of completed motives and finite torsion, not a characteristic-place rank-r separable-point Tate representation or an unrestricted crystalline/étale comparison.
hypotheses: Nilpotent characteristic parameter; residue coefficient algebra F_p; all completion/splitting and effectiveness hypotheses of DM.1/characteristic-local-realization; the exact equal-characteristic category is a recorded input, with a locally free R[[z]]-module and a rank-one R-cokernel killed by z−γ(z).
proofSteps: Identify affine motive restrictions through the elliptic dictionary.
Complete and split coefficient factors; iterate τ by the residue degree.
Apply the same strict finite-group correspondence used in DM.1, retaining connected torsion and its bound.
acceptance: For φ_t=τ² over F, connected length q^(2n) at level t^n is preserved under this comparison.

sources.locator: Theorem 6.4, pp. 24–26; Definition 7.1 and Example 7.2, p. 27; Theorems 7.4 and 7.6, p. 28
sources.match: The finite realization and local completion need the specified characteristic factor and effective Frobenius bound.

importChecks.title: Coefficients of a fixed linear combination
importChecks.statement: For a finite index type I, let v_i∈V be fixed by f and L-linearly independent. If c_i∈L and the vector Σ_i c_i·v_i is fixed by f, then σ(c_i)=c_i for every i. Equality of the constant field with F is not needed for this lemma.
hypotheses: F and L are fields with a specified F-algebra structure on L; no perfection, characteristic-zero, finite-extension or finite-order assumption is made.
V is an L-vector space, also an F-vector space by a compatible scalar tower.
σ is an F-algebra automorphism of L; f is an F-linear endomorphism of V with f(a·v)=σ(a)·f(v). Neither bijectivity of f nor finite dimensionality is assumed unless stated.
proofSteps: Apply f to the finite sum and use additivity, semilinearity and fixedness of each v_i to get Σ_i σ(c_i)·v_i=Σ_i c_i·v_i.
Subtract the two sums. Apply the finite-relation criterion for L-linear independence to the coefficients σ(c_i)−c_i.
acceptance: With the singleton vector 1 in C and conjugation, a fixed coefficient is real.
The empty family gives a vacuous conclusion.
Independence is necessary: with two copies of 1, the zero combination i·1+(−i)·1 is fixed although neither coefficient is fixed.

sources.match: The minimal-relation proof compares a relation between fixed vectors with its coefficient twist; independence forces each coefficient to be fixed. This isolated step works for an arbitrary field automorphism and semilinear map, beyond the analytic pre-t-motive setting of the lemma, and does not yet require identifying the constant field.

importChecks.title: Descent of the span of an independent fixed family
importChecks.statement: Assume exact constants. For a finite L-linearly independent family v_i fixed by f and a fixed vector w, w lies in the L-span of the v_i if and only if it lies in their F-span.
hypotheses: F and L are fields with a specified F-algebra structure on L; no perfection, characteristic-zero, finite-extension or finite-order assumption is made.
V is an L-vector space, also an F-vector space by a compatible scalar tower.
σ is an F-algebra automorphism of L; f is an F-linear endomorphism of V with f(a·v)=σ(a)·f(v). Neither bijectivity of f nor finite dimensionality is assumed unless stated.
The image of F is exactly the fixed field of σ: σ(a)=a if and only if there is c∈F with algebraMap(c)=a.
proofSteps: For the forward implication use Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun to choose L-coefficients of w. The fixed-coefficients lemma makes each coefficient σ-fixed.
Use exact constants to choose coefficients in F. Scalar-tower compatibility turns the same finite sum into an F-linear expression for w.
For the reverse implication, map the F-coefficients into L and use scalar-tower compatibility.
acceptance: Conjugation on C with the singleton family 1 gives precisely the real axis.
With the empty family, a fixed w belongs to either span exactly when w=0.
For σ=id on C with F=R and v=1, w=i is fixed and in the C-span but outside the R-span, demonstrating the exact-constants requirement.

sources.match: In the same relation argument, fixed coefficients belong to the exact constant field F. This gives the intersection of an L-span with fixed vectors as the F-span. The packet abstracts the argument from pre-t-motives to arbitrary semilinear modules, retaining exact constants and independence of the family.

importChecks.title: Independence descent for finite fixed families
importChecks.statement: Assume exact constants. If v:Fin(n)→V is F-linearly independent and each v_i is fixed by f, then v is L-linearly independent, for every n≥0.
hypotheses: F and L are fields with a specified F-algebra structure on L; no perfection, characteristic-zero, finite-extension or finite-order assumption is made.
V is an L-vector space, also an F-vector space by a compatible scalar tower.
σ is an F-algebra automorphism of L; f is an F-linear endomorphism of V with f(a·v)=σ(a)·f(v). Neither bijectivity of f nor finite dimensionality is assumed unless stated.
The image of F is exactly the fixed field of σ: σ(a)=a if and only if there is c∈F with algebraMap(c)=a.
proofSteps: Induct on n. The empty family has no nonzero relation.
Use linearIndependent_finSucc over F to separate the tail and its first vector. By induction the fixed tail is L-linearly independent.
If the first vector were in the L-span of the tail, fixed-span descent would put it in the F-span, contradicting the F-independence criterion. Apply linearIndependent_finSucc over L.
acceptance: n=0 and n=1 are included; in the singleton case independence means the vector is nonzero.
The pair (1,1) over Q is rejected at the independence premise.
The R-independent pair (1,i) is not a fixed family for conjugation, and must not pass as a C-independent family.

sources.match: The lemma proves that a finite F-independent family of fixed vectors remains L-independent by a shortest relation and coefficient descent. The packet isolates this finite step over arbitrary semilinear modules; it needs exact constants, but neither finite dimension nor invertibility of the module map.

importChecks.statement: Assume exact constants. For any index type I, an F-linearly independent family v:I→V whose members satisfy f(v_i)=v_i is L-linearly independent.
hypotheses: F and L are fields with a specified F-algebra structure on L; no perfection, characteristic-zero, finite-extension or finite-order assumption is made.
