proofSteps: Use linearIndependent_iff_finset_linearIndependent to reduce the conclusion to an arbitrary finite subfamily. Restrict F-independence and fixedness to it.
Reindex that finite set by Fin(card) and apply finite-fixed-independence. Transport independence back along the bijection.
acceptance: The theorem has no finite-dimensional hypothesis on V and no finite-order hypothesis on σ.
Exact constants and the fixed-vector premise are independently necessary: σ=id on C fails the former for F=R; conjugation fixes the latter field but not i.
The theorem supplies independence of an arbitrary F-basis of the fixed submodule before its finiteness is known.

sources.match: The source establishes scalar-extension independence of Betti vectors in its analytic setting. The packet extends the finite-relation argument to an arbitrary index set by restricting to finite subfamilies, over arbitrary fields with the specified automorphism and exact constants.

importChecks.title: Injectivity of the Betti comparison map
importChecks.statement: Assume exact constants. Set W=f.fixedSubmodule, using the native F-submodule. The native L-linear map κ=(W.subtype).liftBaseChange L:L⊗_F W→V, given by κ(a⊗w)=a·w, is injective. No finite-dimensional hypothesis is required.
hypotheses: F and L are fields with a specified F-algebra structure on L; no perfection, characteristic-zero, finite-extension or finite-order assumption is made.
V is an L-vector space, also an F-vector space by a compatible scalar tower.
σ is an F-algebra automorphism of L; f is an F-linear endomorphism of V with f(a·v)=σ(a)·f(v). Neither bijectivity of f nor finite dimensionality is assumed unless stated.
The image of F is exactly the fixed field of σ: σ(a)=a if and only if there is c∈F with algebraMap(c)=a.
proofSteps: Choose an F-basis b of W using Module.Free.chooseBasis. Its image in V is F-linearly independent by the native injective inclusion and LinearIndependent.map'. Every image vector is fixed.
Apply fixed-independence to conclude that the image family is L-linearly independent.
Use the native scalar-extended basis b.baseChange L of L⊗_F W. Its i-th vector is 1⊗b_i, whose κ-image is the same image vector.
Identify κ with the linear map prescribed on that basis and apply Module.Basis.injective_constr_of_linearIndependent.
acceptance: For conjugation on C the map C⊗_R R→C is bijective.
For f=2·id on Q the fixed space is zero and κ is injective but not surjective.
For the zero vector space κ is the map between zero spaces.

sources.match: The lemma supplies independence of fixed vectors after extending scalars, and the proposition uses it to inject the scalar-extended Betti space into the analytic motive. The packet expresses that comparison using the native tensor lift; the argument applies to any semilinear module satisfying the stated constant-field hypothesis.

importChecks.title: Finite dimensionality of the fixed submodule
importChecks.statement: Assume exact constants and that V is finite-dimensional over L. Then the native fixed submodule W=f.fixedSubmodule is finite-dimensional over F; V itself is not assumed finite-dimensional over F.
hypotheses: F and L are fields with a specified F-algebra structure on L; no perfection, characteristic-zero, finite-extension or finite-order assumption is made.
V is an L-vector space, also an F-vector space by a compatible scalar tower.
σ is an F-algebra automorphism of L; f is an F-linear endomorphism of V with f(a·v)=σ(a)·f(v). Neither bijectivity of f nor finite dimensionality is assumed unless stated.
The image of F is exactly the fixed field of σ: σ(a)=a if and only if there is c∈F with algebraMap(c)=a.
V is finite-dimensional over L.
proofSteps: Choose an F-basis b of W; include it into V as in betti-comparison-injective.
Use fixed-independence to make it an L-independent family in the finite-dimensional L-space V. LinearIndependent.finite makes its index type finite.
Apply Module.Basis.finiteDimensional_of_finite to the original F-basis of W. This establishes finiteness before any finrank equality criterion is used.
acceptance: Conjugation on C has fixed space of real dimension 1.
Multiplication by 2 on Q has zero-dimensional fixed space.
Finite-dimensionality is proved, not inferred from the numerical value of finrank, which is zero for infinite-dimensional spaces.

sources.match: The proposition bounds the Betti space by the rank of the analytic motive. A chosen F-basis remains L-independent by the preceding lemma, so finite L-dimension makes its index set finite. The packet abstracts this proof without assuming fixed-space finiteness in advance.

importChecks.title: The dimension bound for fixed vectors
importChecks.statement: Assume exact constants and finite-dimensionality of V over L. Then dim_F(f.fixedSubmodule)≤dim_L(V).
hypotheses: F and L are fields with a specified F-algebra structure on L; no perfection, characteristic-zero, finite-extension or finite-order assumption is made.

σ is an F-algebra automorphism of L; f is an F-linear endomorphism of V with f(a·v)=σ(a)·f(v). Neither bijectivity of f nor finite dimensionality is assumed unless stated.

V is finite-dimensional over L.
proofSteps: Use betti-comparison-injective and the native dimension bound for an injective map into V.
Rewrite the dimension of L⊗_F W using Module.finrank_baseChange. The fixed-space-finite lemma separately certifies that this is the dimension of a finite space.
acceptance: Conjugation on C realizes equality 1≤1.
The invertible operator 2·id on Q realizes the strict inequality 0<1.
For the zero space both sides are zero.

sources.match: The proposition bounds the dimension of the Betti space by the motive rank. After proving that the fixed space is finite, native scalar-extension dimension and injectivity give the packet's corresponding inequality for arbitrary finite-dimensional semilinear modules.

importChecks.title: The dimension criterion for the Betti comparison
importChecks.statement: Assume exact constants and finite-dimensionality of V over L. The native comparison κ:L⊗_F f.fixedSubmodule→V is bijective if and only if dim_F(f.fixedSubmodule)=dim_L(V). In the pre-t-motive application this is the numerical criterion for rigid analytic triviality, once the actual scalar field and operator are supplied.
hypotheses: F and L are fields with a specified F-algebra structure on L; no perfection, characteristic-zero, finite-extension or finite-order assumption is made.
V is an L-vector space, also an F-vector space by a compatible scalar tower.
σ is an F-algebra automorphism of L; f is an F-linear endomorphism of V with f(a·v)=σ(a)·f(v). Neither bijectivity of f nor finite dimensionality is assumed unless stated.

V is finite-dimensional over L.
proofSteps: Establish finite-dimensionality of W by fixed-space-finite; a finite F-basis extends to a finite L-basis of L⊗_F W.
The forward implication packages κ as a linear equivalence and uses finrank invariance and Module.finrank_baseChange.

For the reverse implication, base-change dimension makes source and target have equal finite dimension. Use betti-comparison-injective and LinearMap.injective_iff_surjective_of_finrank_eq_finrank to prove surjectivity.
acceptance: Identity on Q and conjugation on C have bijective comparison maps.
The zero-dimensional object is admitted.
The invertible operator 2·id on Q has no nonzero fixed vector and fails surjectivity; invertibility alone does not imply triviality.
The actual DM.8 applicability check still needs L^σ=F_q(t) and the supplied analytic field; this generic criterion does not establish either.

sources.match: The source characterizes rigid triviality by achieving the full rank of the analytic motive. The comparison is already injective; equality of finite dimensions makes it surjective. This linear-algebra consequence is stated for the packet's more general semilinear setting.

importChecks.title: Constant coordinates in a fixed basis
importChecks.statement: Assume exact constants. Let b:I→V be an L-basis indexed by a finite type, with f(b_i)=b_i. For w∈V, f(w)=w if and only if there is a unique family c:I→F with Σ_i algebraMap(c_i)·b_i=w.
hypotheses: F and L are fields with a specified F-algebra structure on L; no perfection, characteristic-zero, finite-extension or finite-order assumption is made.
V is an L-vector space, also an F-vector space by a compatible scalar tower.
σ is an F-algebra automorphism of L; f is an F-linear endomorphism of V with f(a·v)=σ(a)·f(v). Neither bijectivity of f nor finite dimensionality is assumed unless stated.
The image of F is exactly the fixed field of σ: σ(a)=a if and only if there is c∈F with algebraMap(c)=a.
b is an L-basis indexed by a finite type; every basis vector is fixed.
proofSteps: A basis spans V, so express w with L-coefficients. If w is fixed, fixed-coefficients and exact constants lift each coefficient uniquely to F, the latter uniqueness using injectivity of a field embedding.
L-independence of b makes the lifted coefficient family unique by subtracting two expansions.
Conversely, an F-coefficient combination of fixed vectors is fixed by F-linearity.
acceptance: The singleton basis 1 of C with conjugation has exactly real fixed coordinates.
For the empty basis and zero space the unique coefficient function is empty.
This is the coordinate step in the fundamental-solution argument; no analytic matrix or general solution space is newly defined here.

sources.match: The solution-coordinate argument shows that coefficients of a solution relative to a fundamental matrix are fixed by the coefficient automorphism. Together with the fixed-vector lemma, this supplies unique F-coordinates for a fixed L-basis. The packet states this basis consequence abstractly rather than attributing an arbitrary-module theorem to the source.

importChecks.title: Coefficient Frobenius twist
importChecks.statement: Over a perfect characteristic-p field C containing F_q, q=p^m with m>0, let σ be the inverse q-Frobenius automorphism. Extend σ coefficientwise to C[t], C[[t]], C((t)) and rational functions, fixing t; define f^(n) by the n-fold coefficient q-Frobenius for every integer n, so σf=f^(−1). Over C∞ with its multiplicative infinity norm, ||σa||=||a||^(1/q). The twist extends to the radius-one Tate algebra T, its fraction field L and the arithmetic entire ring E, and is an automorphism of each. For entire convergence, inverse twisting replaces the radius r by r^q before taking a q-th root; it is not substitution t↦t^q.
proofSteps: Use the native iterated Frobenius equivalence and its inverse on coefficients.

Apply the native power-series coefficient map and prove its inverse by coefficient extensionality. Restrictedness is preserved because coefficient norms are raised to the positive power 1/q; fraction-ring extension is by its universal property.
acceptance: The series t is fixed, including in positive characteristic.
For an element a not fixed by σ_C, the constant series C(a) is not fixed.
The coefficient twist of (t−a)(t−b) is (t−σ_C(a))(t−σ_C(b)); this distinguishes coefficient twist from substituting t^q.

sources.match: Coefficient q-Frobenius and its integer iterates act on series while leaving the variable t fixed; the negative iterate is inverse coefficient Frobenius. This is the convention used in the difference equation and is represented by the native ring automorphism, not substitution t↦t^q.
The source defines coefficient q-Frobenius on formal series and its integer twists, leaving t fixed; the (-1)-twist is its inverse. This supplies the operator used in the ABP equation.

The consumer sets f^(n) by twisting coefficients through q^n while fixing t, and states its lifting equation with (-1). This independently checks the shared inverse-Frobenius convention, not a new twist construction.
The published coefficient-twist definition agrees with the preprint: integer coefficient Frobenius fixes t, and (-1) denotes the inverse. Its normalization supports the same native automorphism here.

importChecks.title: Algebraic entire series
importChecks.statement: Let C=C∞, k=F_q(θ), and k∞=F_q((1/θ)) with the specified embeddings. E is the subring of C[[t]] consisting of f=Σ a_n t^n whose coefficients are algebraic over k, for which Σ converges at every finite radius, and for which k∞(a_n:n≥0) is finite-dimensional over k∞. The convergence condition is equivalently: for every real r>0, ||a_n|| r^n tends to zero. Evaluation at z∈C is the sum Σ a_n z^n. E embeds in the native radius-one restricted-series subring T.
proofSteps: The finite coefficient-field condition is retained separately from entire convergence. A compositum of two finite coefficient fields controls sums and products.
Use native restrictedness at each positive radius, and completeness plus the ultrametric summability criterion to obtain evaluation as a ring homomorphism.
Algebraicity of each coefficient over k is required for ABP. The larger analytic entire ring in Papanikolas can be distinguished, but this plan uses the ABP subring throughout specialization.
acceptance: Zero is in E and evaluates to zero.
Every constant with an algebraic-over-k coefficient is in E and evaluates to that coefficient.
The series Σ t^n over the chosen C is excluded: its coefficients do not tend to zero at radius one.

sources.match: Papanikolas distinguishes the analytic entire ring by convergence at every radius. The packet deliberately uses the narrower ABP arithmetic subring, adding algebraic-over-k coefficients and a finite coefficient field over k∞; those additional hypotheses come from ABP, not from this analytic definition alone.

The arithmetic entire ring requires coefficients algebraic over k, convergence at every finite radius and finite degree of the coefficient field over k∞. The packet preserves all three conditions and uses evaluation on this ring in lifting.

The published definition has the same arithmetic entire-series conditions: algebraic coefficients, all-radius convergence and a finite coefficient extension of k∞. These are the narrower conditions selected by the packet.

importChecks.title: The one-variable analytic interface
importChecks.statement: T is the existing radius-one restricted-series subring of C∞[[t]], equipped with its Gauss norm; L is its fraction field. The norm is complete, ultrametric and multiplicative. A nonzero f∈T has a finite zero divisor on |t|≤1, and f=λ·P·u with P the monic polynomial of those zeros, u=1+Σ_{n≥1}b_n t^n, sup||b_n||<1 and b_n→0. The corresponding signed divisor gives the same factorization for a nonzero element of L. Thus T is a principal ideal domain, and its maximal ideals are (t−a) with ||a||≤1. These are adaptations of existing restricted-series and Weierstrass theory, not a new Tate-algebra definition.
proofSteps: Reuse current TauCeti.PowerSeries.norm_eq_gaussNorm, norm_coeff_mul_pow_le and norm_le_iff on the native restricted-series subring. Import TauCeti.PowerSeries.IsDistinguished.exists_isUnit_isMonicOfDegree_mul_eq and existsUnique_isUnit_isMonicOfDegree_mul_eq (Weierstrass/Preparation.lean), isUnit_iff_isDistinguished_zero, and TauCeti.PowerSeries.isPrincipalIdealRing_isRestricted_subring (Weierstrass/Ideal.lean). Their complete ultrametric normed-field hypotheses hold for C∞ and radius 1>0. These exports postdate f790474; generic preparation, unit detection and the principal-ideal theorem are existing library results, not new DM.8 or AdicSpaces work.

Over algebraically closed C∞, factor the distinguished polynomial into linear factors. Unit normalization isolates a constant and a strict-norm tail. Pass to fractions to obtain a finite signed zero/pole divisor.
Check the pinned/current discrepancy recorded in the audit before implementation; generic restricted-series theory remains with its existing owner.
acceptance: A factor t−a is a unit exactly when ||a||>1.
A nonzero determinant in L does not imply it is a unit in T.
The constant 1 has no zero divisor and Gauss norm 1.

sources.match: The source defines the radius-one Tate algebra and its fraction field and describes a nonzero element through its zeros and normalized unit. The packet translates that analytic description to the existing restricted-series carrier. Preparation, unit detection and the principal-ideal result are imported from current Tau Ceti; the C∞ zero/pole normalization is the comparison still to supply.

importChecks.title: Limits under positive Frobenius twists
importChecks.statement: For f∈T with Gauss norm at most 1 there exist s≥1 and a polynomial P with coefficients in the algebraic closure of F_q inside C∞ such that f^(ns) tends to P in Gauss norm as n→∞. Moreover P≠0 exactly when ||f||=1. At coefficient level, a with ||a||<1 tends to 0 under a↦a^(q^(ns)); if ||a||=1, an s can be chosen so its residue is fixed and the sequence tends to its unique constant residue representative. The limiting coefficients need not lie in F_q itself.
proofSteps: Use that the residue field is the algebraic closure of F_q; choose a finite common Frobenius period for the finitely many residues in the normalized factorization.
The strict-norm unit tail tends to 1 uniformly. Norm<1 forces the constant factor to 0; norm 1 preserves a nonzero constant factor.
acceptance: For a constant in F_{q^2} not in F_q the limit lies in F_{q^2}, so s=2 can be needed.
A strict-norm series tends to 0.
A radius-one unit of norm 1 has a nonzero polynomial limit.

sources.match: The coefficient lemma makes strictly small coefficients tend to zero and unit coefficients tend to constant residue representatives along a suitable Frobenius subsequence. The series lemma then gives a polynomial limit for norm at most one, nonzero precisely at norm one. Residues lie in the algebraic closure of F_q, so the limit need not have coefficients in F_q itself.

importChecks.title: Exact analytic constant fields
importChecks.statement: For inverse coefficient q-Frobenius σ, T^σ=F_q[t] and L^σ=F_q(t), with the natural polynomial and rational-function embeddings. Also the σ-fixed elements of k̄(t) are F_q(t), and F_q(t)∩T=F_q[t]. The same assertions for σ^n replace F_q by F_{q^n}. These assertions concern the actual C∞ Tate fraction field, not the full formal Laurent-series field, whose constants are F_q((t)).
proofSteps: A fixed restricted series has coefficients in finite F_q and tending to 0; only finitely many are nonzero.
For a fixed fraction the finite polar divisor is σ-stable. Its monic denominator has coefficients in F_q. Multiplying clears poles and reduces to the restricted-series statement.
For a rational function use its normalized numerator/denominator, or compare a monic minimal polynomial for the algebraic-constant extension. Repeat for σ^n.
acceptance: t and 1/(t−1) are fixed fractions.
A fixed formal series with infinitely many nonzero finite-field coefficients is not in T.
F_q(t)∩T contains no element with a pole in the closed disk.

sources.match: The source computes exact constants of the Tate algebra and its fraction field as F_q[t] and F_q(t), using normalized zero/pole factorization; rational functions over bar(k) have the same fixed rational field. Replacing q by q^n gives the higher-power constant fields. Restrictedness excludes infinite constant-coefficient series.

The consumer uses coefficient twisting on the Tate algebra and its fraction field with exact rational constants, alongside its entire ring. This is a use of the shared analytic field interface; its multizeta objects are not additional DM.8 targets.

importChecks.title: Separability of the analytic fraction field
importChecks.statement: The triple F_q(t)⊂k̄(t)⊂L is σ-admissible: σ fixes F_q(t), its restrictions to k̄(t) and L have exact constants F_q(t), and L/k̄(t) is separable in the general field-extension sense. It is not asserted to be finite or algebraic.
proofSteps: The constant-field claims come from analytic-fixed-fields.

Use the characteristic-p separability criterion with the p-basis {t} of k̄(t): in the ambient Laurent series field no p-th root of t exists, since its order would be 1/p. This proves linear disjointness from k̄(t^(1/p)), hence separability. Record the exact criterion as an FA.0 request.
acceptance: Check every field, scalar extension and twist convention in the statement.

sources.match: The source verifies that its analytic field tower is admissible, including separability of the possibly transcendental extension, by the characteristic-p structure of the function variable. The packet records the p-basis/geometric-reducedness route and requests its general field criterion; algebraic IsSeparable would impose an inappropriate extra hypothesis.

importChecks.title: Rigid analytic triviality
importChecks.statement: For a pre-t-motive M supplied by DM.4, let V=L⊗_{k̄(t)}M with its induced semilinear σ operator f, viewed as an F_q(t)-linear endomorphism. Set M^B=fixedSubmodule(f). M is rigid analytically trivial precisely when the native comparison L⊗_{F_q(t)}M^B→V, a⊗v↦av, is bijective. This condition includes surjectivity; an injective comparison is automatic and alone is insufficient.
proofSteps: Reuse native fixedSubmodule and subtype scalar extension; introduce only the bijectivity predicate.
DM.4 supplies the actual motive scalar extension and compatibility with its τ convention; this predicate is meaningful without a new copy of the motive type.
acceptance: The identity on Q has bijective comparison and is rigid trivial.
The zero-dimensional identity is rigid trivial.
Multiplication by 2 on Q is invertible but is not rigid trivial, since its fixed space is zero.

sources.match: Rigid analytic triviality means that scalar extension of the Betti space recovers the analytic motive. The proposition identifies this with the full-rank condition after proving comparison injectivity. The packet uses native comparison bijectivity as its definition, so its dimension characterization is a theorem rather than a substitute definition.

importChecks.title: Fundamental solution matrix
importChecks.statement: For fields F⊂K⊂L with σ-admissible structure and Φ∈GL_r(K), a fundamental matrix is Ψ∈GL_r(L) satisfying σ(Ψ)=ΦΨ, after embedding Φ in L. A rigid analytic trivialization over T is such a matrix in GL_r(T), with equation read in T. A matrix with determinant merely nonzero in L does not meet the integral condition.
proofSteps: Use the native general linear group (matrix units) and an explicit entrywise equation.
The generic definition applies to any coefficient automorphism; the analytic specialization uses inverse q-Frobenius.

The empty identity matrix is fundamental for rank 0.

The motive proposition and solution-coordinate lemma identify its columns with solutions and its inverse with fixed motive coordinates. importChecks.title: Fundamental matrices and Betti bases
importChecks.statement: For M of k̄(t)-dimension r with column basis m and σ(m)=Φ m, M is rigid trivial iff Φ has a fundamental matrix in GL_r(L). If Ψ is one, the entries of Ψ^−1m form an F_q(t)-basis of M^B. The columns of Ψ form an F_q(t)-basis of the vector solution space σ(v)=Φ v; these are two different coordinate conventions.
proofSteps: An inverse fundamental matrix turns the motive basis into fixed vectors. Conversely a fixed L-basis gives a matrix whose inverse solves the equation.
Apply fixed-basis-coordinates for exact constants and uniqueness. Do not identify column solutions with the motive-basis rows without inversion.
acceptance: Check every field, scalar extension and twist convention in the statement.

sources.match: The proposition proves that Ψ⁻¹ times the motive basis is a Betti basis and that rigid triviality is equivalent to existence of a fundamental matrix. This fixes the orientation: solution columns belong to Ψ, but fixed motive vectors use Ψ⁻¹.

importChecks.title: Integral analytic trivializations
importChecks.statement: If a rigid-trivial pre-t-motive has a polynomial σ matrix Φ∈Mat_r(k̄[t]) with det Φ=c(t−θ)^s, c∈k̄^× and s≥0, it has a fundamental matrix Ψ∈GL_r(T). For the corresponding integral DM.4 dual Anderson motive, its T-fixed module is free over F_q[t] of rank r, its basis gives Ψ^−1m, and the integral and rational notions of rigid triviality agree.
proofSteps: Clear denominators of fixed vectors by σ-fixed polynomials, giving an integral fixed lattice with rationalization M^B.

The determinant of a lattice basis is a constant times Ω^s times a polynomial over F_q. If that polynomial has positive degree, a normalized polynomial relation modulo it, its Frobenius limits and a finite-field trace give a smaller-degree fixed relation, contradicting the lattice basis.
Hence the determinant is a T-unit. Use DM.2 Ω and DM.4 freeness/rationalization interfaces.
acceptance: Check every field, scalar extension and twist convention in the statement.

sources.match: For polynomial Φ with determinant supported at t=θ, the proposition clears analytic denominators and produces an invertible Tate-algebra trivialization. It also relates the free integral fixed module over F_q[t] to its rationalization. The later proposition transfers this to the dual Anderson motive; polynomiality alone does not imply eligibility.

importChecks.title: Exact tensor Betti comparison
importChecks.statement: For an exact sequence 0→P→Q→R→0 of pre-t-motives, rigid triviality of Q implies rigid triviality of P and R. On rigid-trivial objects Betti realization is exact and faithful, and the canonical maps P^B⊗_F Q^B→(P⊗_K Q)^B and (P^B)^∨→(P^∨)^B are isomorphisms. Here F=F_q(t), K=k̄(t); tensoring Betti spaces uses F and tensoring motives uses K.
proofSteps: Use left exactness of fixed vectors and scalar-extension exactness. An isomorphism for Q forces the comparisons for the subobject and quotient to be isomorphisms, by injectivity and dimensions.
For faithfulness, a morphism zero on a spanning Betti basis is zero on the scalar extension and therefore on the motive.
Kronecker products of fundamental matrices supply tensor comparison; inverse transposes supply dual comparison. The natural maps, not just equal dimensions, must be identified.
acceptance: Check every field, scalar extension and twist convention in the statement.

sources.match: The propositions prove exactness through subobjects and quotients and compatibility of the Betti functor with tensor products and duals. The packet retains these as combined target-level milestones and corrects the independent tensor-factor ranks in the displayed proof notation, without duplicating the motive constructions owned by DM.4.

importChecks.title: The neutral category of rigid-trivial motives
importChecks.statement: The strictly full subcategory R of the DM.4 pre-t-motive category consisting of rigid-trivial objects is rigid, abelian and F_q(t)-linear; its unit has endomorphism field F_q(t), and ω(M)=M^B is an exact faithful F_q(t)-linear tensor functor to finite-dimensional vector spaces. Thus R is neutral Tannakian over the imperfect field F_q(t). Let T be the strictly full tensor subcategory generated by the rational images of rigid-trivial dual Anderson motives; it too has this fibre functor. T is this generated subcategory, not all effective dual motives and not an assumption that every t-module is trivial.
proofSteps: Import the rigid abelian motive category, its unit, tensor and dual constructions from DM.4. Closure and exactness come from betti-exact-tensor.

Identify End(1) using exact constants. The arbitrary-field neutral reconstruction is already planned as MC.6/neutral-tannaka-reconstruction; instantiate it over F_q(t), with no characteristic-zero assumption.

Define T by the generic tensor-generation construction supplied with MC.6; its chosen generating family is the DM.4 rational image. The effective Frobenius modules of IKLNP are supplied by DM.4 and are not automatically Anderson-free over k̄[σ].

importChecks.title: Admissible difference fields
importChecks.statement: A σ-admissible triple consists of field embeddings F⊂K⊂L, an F-algebra automorphism σ_K of K and an F-algebra automorphism σ_L of L compatible with K→L, exact fixed fields K^σ=L^σ=F, and a separable extension L/K. F is fixed pointwise. No algebraic closure of F, finite extension or characteristic-zero hypothesis is included.
proofSteps: Package only the complete mathematical predicate on specified field and automorphism data.

The embeddings and algebra towers are native. Compatibility is an equation, exact constants are the two explicit range equalities, and separability is expressed by the native geometric-reducedness property for the field extension. It is not Algebra.IsSeparable, which would incorrectly force algebraicity.
acceptance: F=K=L=Q with identity automorphisms is admissible.
F=K=R, L=C with identity on R and conjugation on C is admissible.
The same tower with identity on C is not admissible, because its fixed field is too large.

sources.match: Admissibility consists of a compatible coefficient automorphism on F⊂K⊂L, exact constants F in both K and L, and separability of L/K. The packet records the full tower, using geometric reducedness for the general extension property rather than requiring an algebraic extension.

importChecks.title: The solution space of a difference system
importChecks.statement: For σ-admissible F⊂K⊂L and Φ∈Mat_r(K), Sol(Φ) is the native F-submodule of L^r cut out by σ_L(v)=Φ v. It has F-dimension at most r. If Φ is invertible and Ψ fundamental, every solution is uniquely Ψ c with c∈F^r. For rectangular solution matrices the same description holds columnwise.
proofSteps: The coefficient twist and matrix multiplication are F-linear, so their equalizer is an F-submodule.

For invertible Φ rewrite the equation as fixedness for Φ⁻¹σ and apply the existing fixed-vector chain. For singular Φ, let W be the L-span of solutions. Compatibility gives σ(W)=Φ(W); the coefficient automorphism preserves dim_L W, so Φ restricts to an injection on W. Twisting a minimal relation and cancelling this restricted Φ gives coefficient fixedness, hence F-independence implies L-independence and the bound r. This extends the source's invertible-matrix statement without asserting that Φ is invertible on all L^r.
acceptance: With σ=id, Φ=1 over Q the solution submodule is the whole space.
With σ=id, Φ=2 in rank 1 over Q the solution submodule is zero.
A repeated nonzero solution column is linearly dependent even though each column is a solution.

importChecks.title: The solution ring and field
importChecks.statement: Fix an admissible triple, Φ∈GL_r(K) and Ψ∈GL_r(L) fundamental. Define Σ=K[Ψ_ij, det(Ψ)^−1] as the native K-subalgebra of L generated by these elements, Λ=K(Ψ_ij) as the native intermediate field, and Z=Spec Σ, a closed K-subscheme of GL_r. The evaluation homomorphism K[X_ij, det(X)^−1]→L has image Σ and kernel the defining ideal of Z. Λ is the fraction field of Σ.
proofSteps: Use native adjoin, matrix determinant, localization and spectrum; include the inverse determinant among generators.
The difference equation makes Σ stable under σ and σ inverse. The field generated by matrix entries already contains the inverse determinant.
The generator evaluation gives the quotient/image dictionary and its fraction field.

The diagonal σ action fixes D entrywise, but L⊗_K L need not be a domain. Γ is initially a closed subscheme of GL_r/F; its group structure is a theorem, not part of this definition.

importChecks.title: Invariant ideals descend to constants
importChecks.statement: In L[X_ij, det(X)^−1] let σ_0 act on coefficients and fix the variables. Extension and contraction give inverse bijections between ideals over F and σ_0-stable ideals over L.
proofSteps: Choose a finite-support expression in an F-basis and normalize one coefficient to 1. Subtract twists to reduce support; exact constants complete induction.
acceptance: Check every field, scalar extension and twist convention in the statement.

sources.match: The lemma descends coefficient-twist-stable ideals in a localized polynomial ring from L to the exact constant field using finite-support coefficient relations. The packet expresses the same coefficient argument as a tensor-algebra interface. No solution-ring simplicity or later Σ-descent result is assumed here.

importChecks.title: Difference simplicity of the solution ring
importChecks.statement: The solution ring Σ has no proper nonzero ideal stable under σ; equivalently the kernel of generator evaluation is maximal among proper σ_1-stable ideals, where σ_1 applies coefficient σ and sends X to Φ X. Stability by inclusion suffices because the coordinate ring is noetherian.
proofSteps: Translate by Ψ to turn σ_1 into coefficient σ_0. Extend a putative invariant ideal to a maximal ideal over constants, obtaining a finite field extension E/F and a second fundamental matrix.
Its ratio to Ψ lies in GL_r(E). Noetherian stabilization and faithful flatness of scalar extension force the old defining ideal and the larger one to coincide.
Only the L-valued invariant-ideal clause is used here; the Σ clause is proved afterward, avoiding a logical cycle.
acceptance: Check every field, scalar extension and twist convention in the statement.

sources.match: The corollary proves that the solution ring has no proper nonzero twist-stable ideal using the earlier L-coefficient descent and a constant maximal-ideal specialization. The packet makes the noetherian passage from inclusion stability to equality explicit and imports affine descent without using the later solution-ring ideal-descent theorem circularly.

importChecks.title: Ideal descent over the solution ring
importChecks.statement: Every coefficient-σ-stable ideal in Σ[X_ij, det(X)^−1] is generated by its intersection with F[X_ij, det(X)^−1]. Extension and contraction are inverse on these ideals. This is asserted for the σ-simple solution ring Σ, not for an arbitrary difference algebra.
proofSteps: Use a minimal nonzero support modulo the contracted ideal. Its leading-coefficient ideal is σ-stable and nonzero, so simplicity supplies coefficient 1. Subtract twists and apply exact constants to contradict minimal support.
acceptance: Check every field, scalar extension and twist convention in the statement.

sources.match: The lemma extends invariant-ideal descent from L-coefficients to solution-ring coefficients after σ-simplicity has been established. Finite-support relations and simplicity control the coefficient module. The tensor formulation retains coefficient-only twist and the base-field scalar actions.

importChecks.title: The difference Galois group and its torsor
importChecks.statement: For every admissible triple and fundamental Ψ, Δ admits the Hopf structure inherited from GL_r, with comultiplication D_ij↦Σ_k D_ik⊗D_kj, counit D_ij↦δ_ij and antipode D↦D^−1. Therefore Γ=Spec Δ is a closed F-subgroup scheme of GL_r. Z=Spec Σ is a right Γ_K-torsor: the map (u, v)↦(u, u^−1v) induces Z×_K Z≅Z×_K Γ_K, equivalently an isomorphism Σ⊗_K Σ≅Σ⊗_F Δ. Also Z_L≅Γ_L via u↦Ψ^−1u. These are scheme and coordinate-ring isomorphisms, not just bijections on rational points.
proofSteps: Conjugate defining ideals by the translation X↦Ψ^−1X and use invariant-ideal descent over L and Σ.
The cocycle formula on three tensor factors gives multiplication; identity and factor swap give counit and inverse. Descend the resulting diagrams by faithful flatness.
The field inclusions make Σ faithfully flat over K and F; use the supplier affine descent interface to prove the torsor statement.
acceptance: Check every field, scalar extension and twist convention in the statement.

sources.match: The propositions identify the comparison algebra after base change and construct coproduct, counit and antipode from matrix multiplication, identity and inversion. The theorem proves the solution scheme is a torsor under the resulting affine group scheme. The packet records coordinate-ring isomorphisms and fpqc descent, rather than relying only on rational-point identities.

importChecks.title: Relative algebraic closure in the analytic solution field
importChecks.statement: For the actual analytic triple (F_q(t), k̄(t), L), k̄(t) is algebraically closed in Λ=k̄(t)(Ψ). Namely every element of Λ algebraic over k̄(t) lies in k̄(t). This is a relative-algebraic-closure assertion, not that k̄(t) is an algebraically closed field.
proofSteps: Adjoin all twists of a relatively algebraic element; the resulting intermediate field H is finite and separable over k̄(t), since Λ is finitely generated.
Use the function-field/curve correspondence and a σ-invariant effective divisor above infinity. Riemann–Roch supplies a finite-dimensional stable space of functions generating H.
Apply Lang to GL_m over F_q, base changed to k̄, to produce a σ-fixed basis. Exact constants put every basis function in F_q(t), forcing H=k̄(t).
acceptance: Check every field, scalar extension and twist convention in the statement.

sources.match: For K=bar(k)(t), the proposition turns a finite twist-stable subextension of the solution field into a curve over perfect bar(k). A large divisor gives a finite-dimensional stable section space, Lang normalizes its semilinear action, and exact constants eliminate the extension. The packet separates the curve/Frobenius transport, Riemann–Roch bounds and Lang base extension needed for this proof.

importChecks.title: Smoothness and dimension of the difference group
importChecks.statement: If K is relatively algebraically closed in Λ for an admissible triple, Γ is geometrically integral and smooth over F, Z is geometrically integral and smooth over K, and dim_F Γ=trdeg_K Λ. In the analytic triple the extra hypothesis follows from relative-algebraic-closure. The proof of smoothness uses the finite-type group structure: geometric reducedness alone is not a smoothness criterion for arbitrary schemes.
proofSteps: Separability and relative algebraic closure imply geometric integrality of Σ. Transfer geometric reducedness and irreducibility across the torsor after an algebraically closed extension.
Apply the native finite-type Hopf-algebra smoothness criterion to Γ; smoothness of Z follows by the torsor local trivialization and descent.
Use dimension invariance under field extension and the affine-domain dimension/transcendence theorem for Σ.
acceptance: Check every field, scalar extension and twist convention in the statement.

sources.match: The theorem identifies group dimension with the solution-field transcendence degree and proves smoothness/geometric connectedness in the analytic case; the corollary supplies relative closure there. The packet states the general admissible-field result with relative algebraic closure as an extra hypothesis and uses the native finite-type Hopf-algebra smoothness criterion, not an arbitrary-scheme reducedness shortcut.

importChecks.title: The difference Galois action and its fixed field
importChecks.statement: Right multiplication gives Γ(F)≅Aut_σ(Σ/K)≅Aut_σ(Λ/K). For geometric fixed-field assertions choose an extension of σ to an algebraic closure of L, write F_n for its σ^n-fixed field and assume (F_n, K̄, L̄) is σ^n-admissible for every n and F̄=⋃F_n. On the corresponding geometrically integral solution field Λ̃, the elements fixed by Γ(F̄) are precisely K̄, and Λ∩Λ̃^{Γ(F̄)}=K. The analytic triple has this property. No density of Γ(F) over the imperfect F is assumed.
proofSteps: A σ-commuting automorphism sends Ψ to Ψγ; exact constants imply γ∈GL_r(F), and preserving the solution ring gives γ∈Γ(F).

For a geometric invariant rational function, use SF.0/jacobson-finite-type after extension to an algebraically closed field: closed points of this finite-type scheme are rational and dense. Reducedness and the torsor identity then equate its two pullbacks on their domain of definition, forcing it to be constant.
Use relative algebraic closure to descend the intersection with Λ. Do not replace the union-of-fixed-fields hypotheses by a claim about rational points over F.

importChecks.title: Identification with the motivic Galois group
importChecks.statement: For M∈T with chosen Φ and fundamental Ψ, Γ_Ψ is isomorphic over F_q(t) to Γ_M=Aut^⊗(ω|⟨M⟩). Every N∈⟨M⟩ has a fundamental matrix over Σ; hence Σ_R⊗_F N^B→Σ_R⊗_K N is bijective for every F-algebra R. The induced tensor functor⟨M⟩→Rep_F(Γ_Ψ) is fully faithful, realizes every stable Betti subspace as a submotive, and tensor-generates the representation category. The induced homomorphism is faithfully flat and a closed immersion, hence an isomorphism of group schemes.
proofSteps: Construct the action using Ψ→Ψγ on Σ and the Betti basis Ψ^−1m. Check functoriality on arbitrary F-algebras, not just geometric points.
For fullness reduce Hom(P, N) to Hom(1, Hom(P, N)); invariant coefficient functions descend to K by difference-invariants.
For stable subspaces row-reduce defining equations; uniqueness forces their coefficients to be invariant, hence in K. The block matrix gives a rigid-trivial submotive.
The faithful generator M^B supplies all representations as tensor subquotients. Import MC.6 faithfully-flat and closed-immersion criteria.

importChecks.title: Restricted solutions become entire

proofSteps: Use Lang on Φ(0) to normalize its constant term to 1. The coefficient recursion makes every coefficient algebraic over k.

On the sufficiently small coefficient tail solve inverse-Frobenius differences by convergent sums of positive twists. The fixed difference is zero because it is strictly small. This bounds the coefficient field over k∞.
The same recursion, multiplied by arbitrary C^n, bounds C^n||a_n|| for every C>1, giving infinite radius.

Its proof first gives algebraic coefficients in a finite extension over k∞, then improves convergence at every radius. The packet keeps these conclusions separate and records the Lang normalization input.

The proposition invokes ABP Proposition 3.1.3: a Tate-algebra solution of a polynomial system invertible at zero is entire. The packet also retains ABP's arithmetic coefficient/finite-field conclusions required for the later lifting theorem.

The published proposition proves the same polynomial-system result with invertibility at zero. Its coefficient recursion and convergence argument give both membership in the arithmetic entire ring and the finite coefficient extension used here.

importChecks.title: Arithmetic estimates for relation lifting
importChecks.statement: Let k⊂K_0⊂K⊂k̄ with K_0/k finite separable of degree d, K the perfect closure of K_0 inside k̄, and O its integral closure of A=F_q[θ]. Let size(x) be the maximum of the infinite-place norms of its k-conjugates; use coefficient maxima for matrices and polynomials. Nonzero x∈O satisfies ||x||∞≥size(x)^(1−d). For a nonzero f=Σ a_i z^i∈O[z], any nonzero root λ of multiplicity ν satisfies ||λ||∞^ν≥(max_i size(a_i))^(−d). For C>1 and 0<r<s, a matrix M∈Mat_{r×s}(O), or M∈Mat_{r×s}(O[t]), with size(M)<C has a nonzero kernel vector x over the same ring with size(x)<C^(r/(s−r)). The polynomial statement imposes no fixed degree bound on x.
proofSteps: Collect the precise statements of the five arithmetic input targets; each records its own source and prerequisite chain. No bound on polynomial-kernel degree is added beyond the chosen coefficient cutoff.
acceptance: Check every field, scalar extension and twist convention in the statement.

sources.match: The arithmetic lemmas bound nonzero integral elements using all conjugates over a finite separable coefficient field, bound nonzero polynomial roots, and find small kernel vectors for r<s. These are norm/size estimates on the integral perfect closure, not degree bounds on a polynomial solution. They feed the auxiliary-function proof with the stated strict dimension and nonzero hypotheses.

The published arithmetic lemmas agree with the preprint's conjugate-size lower bound, nonzero-root norm bound and small-kernel-vector estimate for r<s in the integral perfect closure. The packet retains the finite separable coefficient field and the strict size hypothesis.

importChecks.title: Anderson–Brownawell–Papanikolas lifting
importChecks.statement: Let Φ∈Mat_r(k̄[t]) have determinant c(t−θ)^s with c∈k̄^×, s≥0. Let ψ∈E^r satisfy σ(ψ)=Φψ. For every row ρ∈k̄^r with ρψ(θ)=0, there exists a polynomial row P∈k̄[t]^r such that P ψ=0 as an entire function and P(θ)=ρ. The determinant is nonzero and has no roots apart from θ. The coefficients of P need not be constant or lie in F_q[t].
proofSteps: For rank 1 propagate a zero along the distinct inverse-Frobenius orbit of θ; bounded-disk analytic zero finiteness forces the entire function to vanish.

For larger rank clear arithmetic denominators and use the small-kernel estimate to construct bounded-size polynomial rows with a long interval of prescribed orbit zeros. Obtain a bounded-size scalar difference equation for the auxiliary function.
If the auxiliary function never vanishes identically, its leading coefficient has a uniform lower bound by Liouville; Schwarz–Jensen gives an exponentially decreasing upper bound. Contradiction.
Twist a vanishing auxiliary row through adjugate matrices. Its nonzero value at θ lies on the specified ρ-line; rescale to make that value exactly ρ.
For ℓ=1, a zero at θ propagates to θ^(q^(−n)); bounded-disk zero finiteness forces the entire function to vanish.

For ℓ>1 normalize integrally as in ABP §3.4.2 and use the auxiliary-zero target. Since deg h_N<N, at least one h_N^(N+j)(θ) is nonzero for 0≤j<N. Multiply by the positively twisted adjugates; at θ their determinants are nonzero. The resulting polynomial row annihilates ψ and specializes to a nonzero multiple of ρ, so rescale it to obtain exactly P(θ)=ρ.
acceptance: Check every field, scalar extension and twist convention in the statement.

sources.match: For polynomial Φ with det Φ=c(t−θ)^s and an arithmetic entire solution vector ψ, the criterion lifts every algebraic row relation at θ to a polynomial row relation whose value at θ is prescribed. The full proof builds a small auxiliary relation, controls its zeros and forces it to vanish. The packet retains the special determinant, arithmetic coefficients and entire-vector hypotheses.

This theorem recalls ABP lifting with a polynomial matrix whose determinant is a nonzero scalar times a power of t−θ and an entire solution vector. It supplies the specialization interface; the full proof and arithmetic entire conditions are supplied by ABP.

The consumer restates ABP lifting for an arithmetic entire solution vector of the special-determinant polynomial equation. This checks the shared criterion used by its later multizeta relation argument, without moving those specialized applications into DM.8.

The consumer's Theorem 2.2 uses the same special determinant and arithmetic entire vector to lift a row relation at θ to a polynomial relation. It is another application of the shared lifting criterion, not a stronger universal specialization theorem.

The published criterion and complete auxiliary-function proof retain the preprint's polynomial matrix, special determinant, arithmetic entire vector and prescribed row specialization. The packet's lifting statement matches those hypotheses and conclusion.

importChecks.title: Specialization preserves relation rank
importChecks.statement: Under ABP hypotheses, the k̄[t]-rank of the submodule of E generated by the components of ψ equals the k̄-dimension of their specialized span at θ. Equivalently the k̄-dimension of the specialized relation space equals the k̄(t)-dimension of the rational-function relation space. Evaluation of polynomial relation rows is surjective onto all specialized relations.
proofSteps: The polynomial relation kernel is saturated in a finite free module over k̄[t], because its quotient embeds in the domain E and is torsion-free. Thus it is a direct summand; its basis specializes to independent rows.
ABP supplies all specialized relations, giving equality of kernel dimensions and then equality of generated-span dimensions.
The statement is about finite free relation modules; arbitrary specialization of ranks is not claimed.
acceptance: Check every field, scalar extension and twist convention in the statement.

sources.match: The proposition turns ABP lifting into equality of specialized-span dimension and rational-function rank. Its polynomial relation module is saturated and hence a direct summand over the PID bar(k)[t], so a relation basis specializes independently; lifting supplies all specialized relations. It does not assert rank preservation for arbitrary polynomial matrices.

importChecks.title: Bounded monomial spans
importChecks.statement: For a finite family x:I→A in an F-algebra and d≥0, define D_d(x) as the native F-submodule spanned by products∏_i x_i^{e_i} with e:I→N and Σ_i e_i≤d. This includes the constant monomial 1. It is the image of the degree-at-most-d multivariate-polynomial subspace under evaluation, is finite-dimensional, and D_d⊆D_{d+1}. For all entries of Ψ, the vector formed by 1 and all columns of tensor powers Ψ^{⊗n}, 1≤n≤d, spans exactly D_d over K; its specialization spans D_d(Ψ(θ)) over k̄.
proofSteps: Use native polynomial evaluation and exponent functions; repetitions among tensor-entry monomials do not change the span.
The block system is [1] plus Φ^{⊗n} repeated r^n times, with exactly 1+Σ_{n=1}^d r^{2n} coordinates. This formula also works for r=1 and rank 0, avoiding the preprint geometric-series division.
acceptance: D_0 contains 1 even for an empty family.
For the singleton x=0, every D_d is the span of 1.
For a transcendental singleton x, 1, x, x² have dimension 3 in D_2; constants or repeated coordinates alone cannot give this dimension.

sources.match: The period proof places 1 and all bounded-degree tensor-entry monomials in one difference system. Their spans are the generator filtration used for transcendence degree. The packet uses 1+Σₙ₌₁ᵈr²ⁿ as its block length, valid also at rank one and rank zero, instead of the source's geometric quotient that is undefined at rank one.

importChecks.title: Period transcendence degree and Galois dimension
importChecks.statement: Let M∈T have σ matrix Φ∈Mat_r(k̄[t])∩GL_r(k̄(t)) with det Φ=c(t−θ)^s, c≠0, s≥0. Let Ψ∈GL_r(T) have entries in E and σΨ=ΦΨ. Then trdeg_{k̄} k̄(Ψ_ij(θ))=dim_{F_q(t)}Γ_M. Equivalently this equals trdeg_{k̄(t)}k̄(t)(Ψ_ij). Polynomial determinant plus rigid triviality ensures an eligible Ψ exists by integral-trivialization and entire-from-equation. The theorem does not apply to a pre-t-motive lacking such a trivialization.
proofSteps: Construct the bounded tensor-monomial block system. Its determinant remains a nonzero constant times a power of t−θ; its entries are entire.

Specialization-rank equates dim_K D_d(Ψ) and dim_k̄ D_d(Ψ(θ)) for every d. Use the requested SF.0 bounded-generator filtration growth theorem to identify their transcendence degrees, and SF.0/algebraic-scheme-dimension for Krull dimension and field-extension invariance. The dimension theorem alone does not imply the growth comparison.

Difference-smooth-dimension and tannakian-identification identify this dimension with Γ_M. No algebraic-independence conclusion for arbitrary matrix entries is inferred merely from a dimension equality.
acceptance: Check every field, scalar extension and twist convention in the statement.

sources.match: The theorem identifies the transcendence degree of the specialized entire trivialization with the motivic Galois-group dimension. ABP preserves every bounded-monomial span, filtered growth compares transcendence degrees, and the difference/Tannakian comparison identifies the group. The packet retains Ψ∈GL_r(T) and the special polynomial determinant; the suggested field equality now also requires determinant invertibility in T.

importChecks.title: Deformations of small Carlitz logarithms
importChecks.statement: For α∈k̄ with ||α||<q^(q/(q−1)), define L_α(t)=Σ_{i≥0} α^(q^i)/∏_{j=1}^i(t−θ^(q^j)), the empty denominator being 1. It defines a restricted series and converges on ||t||<q^q. It satisfies σ(L_α)=σ(α)+L_α/(t−θ) and L_α(θ)=log_C(α), where log_C is the chosen local inverse supplied by DM.2. L_α itself need not be entire; Ω L_α is entire once its difference system is used.
proofSteps: Each denominator factor has nonzero constant coefficient, so use native formal power-series inversion for its expansion. The norm bound gives coefficientwise and disk convergence of the sum.
Shift the summation index after inverse twist to prove the functional equation; specialization gives the Carlitz logarithm series from DM.2.
acceptance: The zero argument produces the zero series.
For β in the small disk, L_{−β}=−L_β.
For nonzero α in the small disk, L_α has nonzero constant coefficient; the source excludes zero when using the logarithmic extension.

The represented pre-t-motive X fits 0→C→X→1^r→0 in the column-basis convention.

Use entire-from-equation to prove Ω L entries are entire, instead of asserting L itself entire. DM.4 realizes the invertible rational matrix as a pre-t-motive.

importChecks.title: Membership of the logarithm extension in T
importChecks.statement: For the logarithm matrices, X is an object of the chosen category T, not merely of R. Indeed C⊗X is the rationalization of a rigid-trivial dual Anderson motive M over k̄[t], with σ matrix (t−θ)Φ. It lies in 0→C^{⊗2}→M→C^r→0; it is finite free over k̄[t] and k̄[σ], and (t−θ)^n M⊂σ M for n≥2. Since T contains C^∨ and is closed under tensor products, X∈T.
proofSteps: The explicit σ matrix gives the exact sequence and the power-annihilation condition.
Import DM.4 finite generation and freeness over k̄[σ] for this lattice, including ABP Proposition 4.3.2; do not manufacture freeness from the polynomial rank alone.
The fundamental matrix and integral/rational criterion give rigid triviality; tensor with C^∨ yields X.
acceptance: Check every field, scalar extension and twist convention in the statement.

sources.match: The proposition proves that X belongs to the tensor category generated by dual Anderson motives by showing C⊗X is such a motive. It checks polynomial and σ-module finite freeness and the nilpotence condition using the ABP criterion. The packet requires this σ-generation argument; polynomial freeness of X alone would not suffice.

The criterion gives finite freeness over the skew polynomial ring from the polynomial-module structure and the sufficiently strong (t−θ)-nilpotence condition. Papanikolas checks it for C⊗X, supplying the dual Anderson membership needed here.

The published criterion has the same polynomial-module and nilpotence hypotheses and yields skew-polynomial finite freeness. It validates the σ-generation step for C⊗X rather than treating polynomial freeness as motive membership.

importChecks.title: The Carlitz motivic Galois group
importChecks.statement: For the Carlitz object C with σ matrix t−θ and fundamental Ω, Hom_T(C(m), C(n)) is F_q(t) for m=n and zero otherwise, and Γ_C≅G_m over F_q(t). The distinction between weights uses Ω∉C∞(t), which follows from its infinitely many zeros. In particular the Carlitz period π̃=−1/Ω(θ) is transcendental over k̄ by period-transcendence.
proofSteps: The one-dimensional difference equation for Hom(C(m), C(n)) has solutions constant times Ω^{m−n}. A nontrivial power of Ω has infinitely many zeros or poles, so is not rational.

The generated category is the integer-weight graded finite-dimensional category over F_q(t). Instantiate MC.6/neutral-tannaka-reconstruction and the requested graded-category computation of its group as G_m.
Apply period-transcendence to the eligible rank-one Carlitz matrix.
acceptance: Check every field, scalar extension and twist convention in the statement.

sources.match: The source computes morphisms between Carlitz tensor powers and identifies their generated category with integer-weight graded F_q(t)-vector spaces, giving G_m as the Carlitz group. Ω has infinitely many zeros, and period specialization gives Carlitz-period transcendence. The packet corrects the printed graded coefficient field and imports general reconstruction instead of rebuilding it.

The rank-one application specializes the entire Carlitz function and derives transcendence of the Carlitz period from lifting and its infinitely many zeros. This supports the period normalization/transcendence input, not the separate Tannakian graded-category computation.

The published rank-one application gives the same Carlitz-period transcendence argument and Ω specialization. Its role is the analytic transcendence input; the graded-category G_m computation is in Papanikolas.

importChecks.title: The linear Carlitz logarithm kernel
importChecks.statement: For the logarithm object X, Γ_X is a smooth geometrically connected closed subgroup of G={[[a, 0], [v, I_r]]:a invertible}. The projection a gives a faithfully flat homomorphism π:Γ_X→G_m. Its kernel V is a vector subspace of G_a^r over F_q(t), as a group scheme, and π is smooth. A proof must establish separability of this particular projection before claiming V is smooth. This does not follow for an arbitrary surjective morphism of smooth groups. Consequently if F_1, …, F_s are homogeneous linear forms defining V and γ=(b_0, b)∈Γ_X(F) with b_0∉F_q, the ideal of Γ_X is generated by G_i=(b_0−1)F_i(v)−F_i(b)(a−1).
proofSteps: The comparison matrix places Γ_X in G; the subobject C makes π faithfully flat. Scalar conjugation preserves V.

Over a perfect closure, verify the particular scalar-action projection is separable. Then V is smooth, its geometric points are stable under all scalars, and their closure is a linear space. Descend its linear ideal. The verification of separability is recorded as an explicit gap rather than treating all smooth group surjections as smooth.

Once V is a vector group, its representable fpqc torsor over the field is fppf locally trivial because it is smooth of finite presentation. Apply SF.2/abelian-torsor-h1 and quasi-coherent-topology-comparison to O^r on Spec F: H¹_fppf(F,G_a^r)=0. Thus each fibre of π over an F-point has an F-point. Choose b_0 outside F_q, and use its cyclic closure and translation by V to obtain the displayed linear equations. This does not assert splitting for an arbitrary unipotent kernel.
acceptance: Check every field, scalar extension and twist convention in the statement.

sources.match: The source analyzes the scalar-triangular group of the logarithm motive and proves its kernel is linear before constructing a rational lift and a dense cyclic subgroup. The packet limits this to that particular group: it retains the open separability/Lie-surjectivity verification and uses vector-group torsor splitting only after the kernel is proved vectorial.

importChecks.title: Linear relations and logarithm group dimension
importChecks.statement: Let N be the k=F_q(θ)-linear span of π̃, log_C(α_1), …, log_C(α_r) for small algebraic arguments. Then dim_F Γ_X=dim_k N. More precisely each linear form F=Σ c_i v_i defining V and γ=(b_0, b_i) as above yields (b_0(θ)−1)Σ c_i(θ)log_C(α_i)−Σ c_i(θ)b_i(θ)π̃=0, and these span all k-linear relations. Evaluation F_q(t)→F_q(θ) is denominator-safe since θ is transcendental over F_q; the auxiliary rational torsor coefficient is separately proved regular at θ.
proofSteps: The linear G_i equations translate to torsor equations H_i=G_i−f_i a. A σ equation propagates any putative pole of f_i at θ along an infinite twist orbit; hence f_i and its twist are regular there.
Divide the torsor equation by Ω and evaluate using π̃=−1/Ω(θ). Independent linear forms provide r+1−dim Γ_X independent k-linear relations.
Conversely trdeg≤linear-span dimension, while period-transcendence gives this trdeg=dim Γ_X. Equality proves completeness of the relations.
acceptance: Check every field, scalar extension and twist convention in the statement.

sources.match: The theorem identifies the logarithm-group dimension with the k-linear span dimension of the Carlitz period and small logarithms. Constant rational-function relations are evaluated at θ after denominator descent, and pole propagation controls rational coefficients in the converse direction. The packet keeps k-linearity distinct from bar(k)-algebraic independence.

importChecks.title: Reduction to small algebraic logarithms
importChecks.statement: For λ∈C∞ with exp_C(λ)∈k̄^×, there exist n≥0, α∈k̄^× with ||α||<q^(q/(q−1)), and f∈F_q[θ] such that λ=θ^n log_C(α)+f π̃. If exp_C(λ)=0, λ itself lies in F_q[θ]π̃. Thus any finite family of logarithms with algebraic exponentials is contained in the k-linear span of π̃ and finitely many small principal algebraic logarithms.
proofSteps: If the exponential is already small, take it as α and n=0; otherwise solve θ x+x^q=β repeatedly in k̄. Newton polygon bounds shrink division points until the local inverse applies.
Carlitz equivariance gives exp_C(θ^n log_C(α))=exp_C(λ); the kernel period lattice gives f π̃.
Handle exp_C(λ)=0 separately; the printed nonzero-exponential lemma alone cannot cover such λ.
acceptance: Check every field, scalar extension and twist convention in the statement.

sources.match: For an arbitrary logarithm with nonzero algebraic exponential, the lemma divides by a large power of θ until the principal logarithm is small and expresses the remaining ambiguity as a k-multiple of the Carlitz period. The packet treats zero exponentials separately by the period kernel, because the division lemma does not cover them.

importChecks.title: Algebraic independence of Carlitz logarithms
importChecks.statement: Let λ_1, …, λ_r∈C∞ with exp_C(λ_i)∈k̄ for all i. If this family is linearly independent over k=F_q(θ), it is algebraically independent over k̄. The linear field is k, not k̄. There is no fixed choice of principal branch for arbitrary λ_i. A nonzero period with exponential zero is eligible. The result is only for Carlitz logarithms, not for all higher-rank Drinfeld modules.
proofSteps: Reduce to a finite-dimensional k-space N generated by the period and small principal logarithms. The previous two theorems give trdeg_{k̄}k̄(N)=dim_k N.

Choose a k-basis of N; its size equals the transcendence degree, so it is algebraically independent over k̄. Extend the given independent family to such a basis using an invertible k-linear change of coordinates.
Discarding extra basis vectors preserves algebraic independence. This argument handles zero-exponential periods and avoids an incorrect nonzero-only reduction.
acceptance: A single nonzero Carlitz logarithm with algebraic exponential is transcendental, including π̃.
The pair(λ, λ) fails the linearity hypothesis and has polynomial relation X_1−X_2.
An invertible pre-t-motive with no analytic trivialization cannot be used to assert period independence.

sources.match: The theorem deduces bar(k)-algebraic independence of k-independent Carlitz logarithms with algebraic exponentials by reducing to a basis of the span containing the period and principal logarithms. The packet explicitly supplies the zero-exponential period case missing from the cited division step and uses basis extension rather than assuming the chosen logarithms span the whole space.

importChecks.title: Frobenius-invariant common denominators
importChecks.statement: Let Φ_i∈Mat_{r_i}(k̄[t]) have det Φ_i=c_i(t−θ)^{s_i}, c_i≠0, s_i≥0, i=1, 2. If B∈Mat_{r_1×r_2}(k̄(t)) satisfies σ(B)Φ_2=Φ_1B, its monic least common denominator belongs to F_q[t]. Thus a nonzero polynomial over F_q clears all entries. The matrix B is rational; the polynomial domain printed in CPY Proposition 2.2.1 is corrected in source issue E-DM8-8, reusing PAPER-NGODAC-21/E10.
proofSteps: The denominator of σ(B) divides den(B)(t−θ)^{s_2}. If it has a pole at θ, repeated Frobenius shifts force infinitely many distinct poles, using both determinant conditions.
Therefore the monic denominator is σ-fixed and lies in F_q[t]. This also proves rationalized Hom compatibility for DM.4 without redefining the motives.
acceptance: Check every field, scalar extension and twist convention in the statement.

sources.match: The proposition shows that the monic least common denominator of a rational motive morphism is fixed by inverse Frobenius and hence lies in F_q[t], using both polynomial matrices with determinant supported at θ. The packet keeps rational matrix entries before clearing denominators; the result does not claim every rationalized morphism is polynomial.

The proof transports a morphism between rationalized motives to a constant matrix using their fundamental solutions, then uses determinant support to force its monic denominator into F_q[t]. The printed polynomial type for the starting matrix is corrected to rational entries, as confirmed by the 1/t identity example.

In the auxiliary block argument, constant solution coordinates and a rational basis change lead to denominator descent over F_q[t]. This is a concrete consumer of the shared rational-matrix lemma, not a claim that the starting morphism has polynomial entries.
